entries.content: --- id: "i18n" name: "i18n Rules — projects with message catalogs" kind: "rule" description: "Applies to any repo with an i18n feature: message catalogs (`{vi,en}` per namespace), multi-locale UI, locale-aware translators (next-intl, custom `useI18n`). Consumers WITHOUT i18n must omit this file. Includes this file for any repo that ships user-facing strings through a catalog." scope: "Projects with message catalogs, multi-locale UI, user-facing copy" priority: "mandatory" --- # i18n Rules — projects with message catalogs 0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies. Applies to any repo with an i18n feature: message catalogs (`{vi,en}` per namespace), multi-locale UI, locale-aware translators (next-intl, custom `useI18n`). Consumers WITHOUT i18n must omit this file. Includes this file for any repo that ships user-facing strings through a catalog. ## Scope Catalog discipline: where strings live, locale parity, interpolation limits, what is deliberately NOT translated, and which words a message may use. ## Catalog ownership (mandatory) 1. **Every UI string lives in the catalog** — messages live in `packages/i18n/src/messages/{vi,en}/.json` (one file per namespace per locale, merged at a shared `locales.ts`). Components use the app translator (`useTranslations` on next-intl apps, `useI18n()` on the miniapp) and render `t('.key')`. A hardcoded string in a file that already calls `t()` is still a violation — sweep stragglers, not just files with no translator. When converting, reuse existing keys before adding new ones; never ship a second key for the same string. 2. **en ≡ vi parity is a build rule** — every new key goes into BOTH locale files in the same commit. A parity test (en ≡ vi key sets) guards it; missing keys return the key itself at runtime, so a bare key is a typo signal, not a fallback. 3. **Interpolation only, no rich text** — the miniapp translator substitutes `{name}` placeholders only; it does not render markup. For emphasis inside a message, split the message so the styled segment arrives as a param value and wrap the param in JSX: `t('court.cancelFree', { days: '≥ 2 ngày' })` rendered inside `{days}`. Next-intl apps may use `t.rich` where the message needs inline markup. 4. **Label maps hold keys, not strings** — when display labels live in a data/constant map (`AMENITY`, `BOOKING_STATUS`, status/sort enums), the map stores i18n keys (`'courtList.amenityLight'`), never user-facing text, and the render site calls `t(label as I18nKey)` (the typed key union). Translation happens at the render boundary, not inside data. 5. **Not everything is chrome** — do not translate: content (articles, wiki, help pages), demo/mock data, proper nouns (venue names, zones, cities, person names), locale labels (`Tiếng Việt`), currency suffixes (`đ`) and other formatting (use the shared `vnd()`/`VND()` formatters), and strings embedded in API payloads (`desc` fields) — those are data, not UI. Dead label maps with no consumers are not an i18n gap; fix or delete them, don't translate them. 6. **Never pass a possibly-undefined key to the translator** — `t(key)` throws deep inside the translator implementation when `key` is `undefined` — not a graceful no-op, not a caught React error, a crash. A fallback chain (`a?.b ?? c?.d`) that can bottom out at `undefined` must resolve to a real key before it reaches `t()`: ```ts // Bad — throws when both sides are unset tr(FORMATS[x]?.label ?? x); // Good — always resolves to a real key tr(FORMATS[x]?.label ?? "fallback.key"); ``` Proven by a real incident: `tr((FORMATS[t.stageTwo?.format || '']?.label ?? t.stageTwo?.format) as I18nKey)` crashed the whole screen whenever `t.stageTwo` was `null` (a field that was, in practice, never populated) — the `??` chain bottomed out at `undefined`, not a string. ## User-facing copy (mandatory) 6a. **User-facing copy scope** — Apply these requirements to copy work: Rules for writing or rewriting message values. A copy pass edits values only: keys and every `{placeholder}` stay intact. Dead keys stay dead — delete them or leave them, re-polishing them only launders copy nobody renders. 7. **A message names the outcome and the next step, never the machinery** — users read what happened and what to do ("Đang xác nhận thanh toán, tự cập nhật trong vài giây"), in their own words. Internal vocabulary stays out of every message value: integration names and mechanics (webhook, HMAC, VA, memo, feed, "qua SePay VietQR" on customer payment buttons), process codes (SLA, SOP, RLS, WORM, CAS, k-anonymity), architectural nouns ("Cổng Phụ huynh / Portal" → use "Trang Phụ huynh" or "Góc Học tập"), B2B accounting jargon on personal earnings ("Giải ngân", "Đối soát" → use "Chuyển thu nhập", "Đã nhận"), unsubstantiated marketing percentages ("98% phù hợp" → use "Gợi ý phù hợp"), and raw enums or status codes (precedent: Gia Su Anh Minh 2026-10). The term table (rule 8) is the exemption register: it may sanction the familiar customer word for a mechanism ("VA" → "tài khoản ảo" — the term SePay's own customers use) or keep a brand name as-is ("Zalo OA"); keeping or translating is the table's call, not each string's. A provider name earns its place only where the user acts inside that provider's own UI (e.g. "dán vào mục Webhooks của SePay"). 8. **One term table per product (`DESIGN.md`)** — root `DESIGN.md` (or `GLOSSARY.md` in repos without `DESIGN.md`) carries the User-Facing Copy **Term table** mapping each internal term to its displayed VI and EN form (e.g. Paddle DNA → "Gu vợt", Price Bank → "Giá tham khảo", Match Score → "Gợi ý phù hợp", Contact Gate SLA → "Phản hồi trong 2 giờ"), while keeping `GLOSSARY.md` strictly a pure domain glossary (`rules/frontend.md` #21). Write from the table; add a new display term to `DESIGN.md` in the same change that uses it. A string that contradicts the table is a violation even when it reads well. 9. **VI leads, EN mirrors** — draft the VI value first, then mirror `en` in the same commit (rule 2). Keep English only for brand/product names and sport or industry terms with no common VI equivalent (dink, kitchen, sweet spot); give each a short VI gloss at first use ("vùng bếp (kitchen)"). Never leave raw English UI loanwords (`Dashboard`, `Verify`, `Profile`, `Streak`, `Badge`, `Feedback`, `Support`, `Submit`, `Cohort`) in VI copy when a natural Vietnamese word exists (`Tổng quan`, `Xác thực`, `Hồ sơ`, `Chuỗi ngày học`, `Huy hiệu`, `Nhận xét`, `Hỗ trợ`, `Nộp bài`, `Lớp nhóm`). One term, one translation, everywhere: a term rendered three different ways across files is one drift bug, not three wordings. 10. **A translated label stands alone (including Admin Console chrome)** — no code, enum, or original parked in parentheses beside it, in any language. "Đủ đôi (PAIRED)", "Đang học (ACTIVE)", "Trạng thái: PENDING_PAYMENT", "409 · SCHEDULE_CONFLICT", "Ảnh bìa (tải trực tiếp)", "Khu dân cư (không bắt buộc)", "Ghi chú (tùy chọn)" are leaks of the internal name or an explanation the label does not need; the machine value lives in the key or the payload, the label holds the human reading, and detail moves to a hint, placeholder, or full sentence *without* parentheses. Placeholders count as labels: `placeholder="Ghi chú (tùy chọn)"` is the same violation as a label. Even in an operator/Admin Console, navigation tabs, buttons, status badges, and modal titles use human labels (`Học thử & Phản hồi`, `Đang học`, `Đã phân công`, `Chờ duyệt` — never `Dạy thử & SLA` or `Đang học (ACTIVE)`); raw enum or reference codes appear only inside monospace technical reference cells (`font-mono`) or audit log filter chips. The ban is mechanical: a grep for `(` inside a message value or a `placeholder=`/`Label` child flags it. 11. **Policy numbers live once** — refund, cancel, and cutoff copy states its days and percentages from a single source, and every surface repeating the policy repeats the same numbers. Two keys disagreeing ("hủy trước 4 giờ" vs "≥ 2 ngày") is a bug to fix at the source, not a wording choice. - **Statutory retention and dispute clauses live in `/terms` and `/privacy`, never in checkout/KYC chrome** — legal retention periods (7-year accounting ledger retention, KYC document storage policies, 24h dispute window mechanics) belong in the canonical Terms & Privacy documents, kept in sync across Web MDX (`apps/web/src/content/legal/`) and Miniapp legal tabs (`legal-screen.tsx`), never inline on transactional forms or upload widgets where compliance boilerplate creates user anxiety (precedent: Ecopick 2026-10, PR #452). 12. **Error catalogs are sentences** — each `errors.json` value tells the result and the next step in the user's language ("Khung giờ này đã đầy, chọn khung khác nhé"); the error code does its work as the key only. 13. **Server-sent copy follows the same rules** — strings that reach users through API payloads (quiz questions, challenge and tier names, notification templates, seed data, validation messages, error strings) are user-facing copy living outside the catalog, and a catalog-only pass misses them. Widen any copy audit or rewrite to seed files, template constants, hardcoded data modules, and API message strings, not just `messages/`. Parentheses in those strings are the same violation as in labels (rule 10). 14. **A sweep closes the rewrite (catalogs + `.ts`/`.tsx` source scan in `leak.test.ts`)** — the change is done when a grep over the touched catalogs AND `.ts`/`.tsx` source files returns nothing: the internal terms from rule 7, the banned internal names of the product's own term table in `DESIGN.md`, and parenthesized explanations or codes in any message value or `placeholder=`/`Label` child (rule 10). Extend the sweep over the e2e spec corpus — specs that assert literal copy strings break on the rename (`rules/e2e-testing.md` rule 8). Wire both the catalog sweep and the source-tree `.ts`/`.tsx` scan (`apps/*/src`, `packages/ui`, `packages/auth`) as test cases in `packages/i18n/tests/leak.test.ts` so CI rejects both catalog leaks and hardcoded JSX regressions from `.dc.html` porting (precedent: Gia Su Anh Minh 2026-10). 15. **Long copy contracts with `&`** — a message value of ≥ 40 characters uses `&` where it would say "và"/"and" ("Tạo & quản lý giải đấu"); short labels keep the word, where the glyph saves no row and reads rough. The rule is mechanical, so enforce it with the same scripted pass as any bulk rename, at space/word boundaries only. 16. **A non-Next SPA keeps the miniapp catalog shape** — `next-intl` needs Next.js. A Vite/React app puts messages at `src/i18n/messages/{vi,en}/.json` (one file per namespace per locale) behind a small `useI18n()` hook, and the same two build rules apply unchanged: `en ≡ vi` key sets with a parity test (rule 2), and every display term written from the term table in the repo glossary (rule 8). The locale default is the audience's, not the framework's. ## Generated catalog metadata (mandatory) 18. **Generate the namespace index and error-code registry from `messages/*/*.json`** — A script writes both generated files from the JSON source, checks that `vi` and `en` carry the same namespaces and deep leaf keys, and supports `--check`. Run `--check` in lint/CI so a new namespace or a stale index fails the gate. A hand-written 80-import `locales.ts` is a registry that will drift. 19. **One `Locale` type** — The catalog owns `LOCALES` and `Locale`; legal, contracts, and app cookies import that type. Never redeclare `'vi' | 'en'`, and never widen a locale parameter to `string` to avoid threading the type. 20. **Display labels live in the catalog, not shared types** — A shared `types` package carries category values, status codes, and wire shapes. It never carries user-facing labels. The render site maps the value to a catalog key (`rules/i18n.md` #4). 21. **Keep scoped keys scoped** — A component under a namespace stores `KeysOf<'ns'>` keys (`tabs.vendor`), not full catalog keys. Do not widen the map to the global `MessageKey` only to delete a cast; store the namespaced key and let `t` accept it directly. 22. **The error-code union derives from the catalog** — Generate `ERROR_CODES` from `errors.json`; the API's `ErrorCode` type aliases the generated list. Do not maintain a third list in `@repo/types`, and do not keep a coverage test that compares a generated file with the catalog it came from. ## React-dependent helpers in pure packages 22a. **React helper entry point** — Keep React-dependent helpers separate: - **Entry-point split**: when a pure package (e.g. `@giasuanhminh/i18n`) needs React hooks, put them in a separate entry point (`client.ts`) with its own `exports["./client"]` and add `react`/`@types/react` to that package's deps. Consumers import `@scope/pkg/client`. Keeps the server surface pure. Precedent: giasuanhminh `useApiErrorMessage` centralization 2026-10. ## Catalog isolation (mechanical) 17. **Client entry points never import catalog values** — `@scope/i18n/locales`, `client.tsx`, and any client-importable module must not import `src/catalog` (or any module that imports message JSON). Catalog values (`catalog`, `keys`, `appCatalog`) live in server/catalog modules only; enforce with a depcruise or `no-restricted-imports` rule so the leak cannot recur. Precedent: VibeHost 2026-10 bundle audit.

entries.title: Issue Rules — grouping, umbrella mechanics & PR closing
entries.name: Issue Rules — grouping, umbrella mechanics & PR closing
entries.description: Applies to every repo that uses GitHub Issues as its tracker.
entries.scope: Repos with a GitHub issue tracker

rules.title: Module context
rules.content:
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to every repo that uses GitHub Issues as its tracker.

rules.title: Search before creating
rules.content: 1. **Search before creating** — List open issues first (`gh issue list --state open --json number,title`). If an open issue or umbrella already covers the scope, extend it instead of creating a duplicate.

rules.title: One umbrella issue per effort, never one per finding
rules.content: 2. **One umbrella issue per effort, never one per finding** — An audit or cleanup producing 25 related findings becomes **one** umbrella issue with acceptance criteria grouped per surface (`api`, `web`, `portal`, `miniapp`), not 25 issues.

rules.title: Split only for independent delivery
rules.content: 3. **Split only for independent delivery** — Create separate issues only when each slice is independently grabbable, demoable alone, and shares no boundary, milestone, or owner with the rest.

rules.title: Link existing issues as native sub-issues instead of closing them
rules.content:
4. **Link existing issues as native sub-issues instead of closing them** — Keep overlapping open issues open with their own labels/blockers, link them natively, and annotate the umbrella checklist item with `covered by #n`:

   ```sh
   gh issue edit <parent> --add-sub-issue <n>
   ```

rules.title: Close only truly superseded issues
rules.content:
5. **Close only truly superseded issues** — When an umbrella completely replaces an older issue, close the old one as a duplicate pointing to the umbrella:

   ```sh
   gh issue close <n> --reason duplicate --comment "Superseded by #<umbrella>"
   ```

rules.title: Record dependencies via native `blocked-by` edges
rules.content:
6. **Record dependencies via native `blocked-by` edges** — Wire blocking relationships in the graph, not just in prose:

   ```sh
   gh issue edit <n> --add-blocked-by <m>
   ```

rules.title: Label every touched surface
rules.content: 7. **Label every touched surface** — Attach one `sub-product:*` label per affected app plus `type:feature` / `type:chore`, `priority`, and `ready-for-agent` when the body is self-contained.

rules.title: Keep the closing keyword immediately adjacent to `#N`
rules.content: 8. **Keep the closing keyword immediately adjacent to `#N`** — Write `Closes #N` (or `Fixes #N` / `Resolves #N`) in the PR body. Intervening words (`Resolves the buildable slice of #5`) break GitHub's auto-close parser and leave the issue open after merge (Precedent: RestoSuite #35). When a parent issue's remaining scope moved to sub-issues, close the parent manually with pointers (`gh issue close N --reason completed --comment "..."`).

rules.title: Never auto-close a parent issue from a partial PR
rules.content: 9. **Never auto-close a parent issue from a partial PR** — A PR delivering one slice of an umbrella writes `Part of #N`; the parent closes only when all sub-issues are complete.

# Issue Rules — grouping, umbrella mechanics & PR closing

<!-- rule: module-context -->
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to every repo that uses GitHub Issues as its tracker.

## Grouping

<!-- rule: search-before-creating -->
1. **Search before creating** — List open issues first (`gh issue list --state open --json number,title`). If an open issue or umbrella already covers the scope, extend it instead of creating a duplicate.
<!-- rule: one-umbrella-issue-per-effor -->
2. **One umbrella issue per effort, never one per finding** — An audit or cleanup producing 25 related findings becomes **one** umbrella issue with acceptance criteria grouped per surface (`api`, `web`, `portal`, `miniapp`), not 25 issues.
<!-- rule: split-only-for-independent-d -->
3. **Split only for independent delivery** — Create separate issues only when each slice is independently grabbable, demoable alone, and shares no boundary, milestone, or owner with the rest.

## Umbrella mechanics

<!-- rule: link-existing-issues-as-nati -->
4. **Link existing issues as native sub-issues instead of closing them** — Keep overlapping open issues open with their own labels/blockers, link them natively, and annotate the umbrella checklist item with `covered by #n`:

   ```sh
   gh issue edit <parent> --add-sub-issue <n>
   ```

<!-- rule: close-only-truly-superseded -->
5. **Close only truly superseded issues** — When an umbrella completely replaces an older issue, close the old one as a duplicate pointing to the umbrella:

   ```sh
   gh issue close <n> --reason duplicate --comment "Superseded by #<umbrella>"
   ```

<!-- rule: record-dependencies-via-nati -->
6. **Record dependencies via native `blocked-by` edges** — Wire blocking relationships in the graph, not just in prose:

   ```sh
   gh issue edit <n> --add-blocked-by <m>
   ```

<!-- rule: label-every-touched-surface -->
7. **Label every touched surface** — Attach one `sub-product:*` label per affected app plus `type:feature` / `type:chore`, `priority`, and `ready-for-agent` when the body is self-contained.

## PR close link

<!-- rule: keep-the-closing-keyword-imm -->
8. **Keep the closing keyword immediately adjacent to `#N`** — Write `Closes #N` (or `Fixes #N` / `Resolves #N`) in the PR body. Intervening words (`Resolves the buildable slice of #5`) break GitHub's auto-close parser and leave the issue open after merge (Precedent: RestoSuite #35). When a parent issue's remaining scope moved to sub-issues, close the parent manually with pointers (`gh issue close N --reason completed --comment "..."`).
<!-- rule: never-auto-close-a-parent-is -->
9. **Never auto-close a parent issue from a partial PR** — A PR delivering one slice of an umbrella writes `Part of #N`; the parent closes only when all sub-issues are complete.

entries.title: Library Baseline — one library per concern, chosen by framework
entries.name: Library Baseline — one library per concern, chosen by framework
entries.description: Applies to every TypeScript/JavaScript project. One library per concern, fixed by framework. A substitute library is a violation, not a preference. Reach for this table first, then verify the chosen library's current API via Rule 7 before writing calls.
entries.scope: All TS/JS projects

rules.title: Library baseline: core concerns
rules.content:
0a. **Library baseline: core concerns** — Use the applicable baseline in this table.

Applies to every TypeScript/JavaScript project. One library per concern, fixed by framework. A substitute library is a violation, not a preference. Reach for this table first, then verify the chosen library's current API via Rule 7 before writing calls.

## The table

| Concern                | Web/React (portal, web, mobile-rn)                                                                  | NestJS (`apps/api`)                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| HTTP client            | `axios` (`rules/frontend.md` #1, #11)                                                               | `@nestjs/http-client` (`rules/nestjs.md` #21)                                                        |
| Runtime validation     | `zod`                                                                                               | `class-validator` + `class-transformer` (`zod` only for boot `env.schema.ts`, `rules/nestjs.md` #18) |
| Forms                  | `react-hook-form` + `@hookform/resolvers/zod`                                                       | —                                                                                                    |
| Server state           | `@tanstack/react-query`                                                                             | —                                                                                                    |
| AI models, agents      | `@ai-sdk/react` `useChat` for chat UI                                                               | `@nestjs/ai` (`AiModule` + `AiService` + `@AgentFunction` — `rules/nestjs-ai.md`)                    |
| Time                   | `date-fns` + `@date-fns/tz` (`rules/general.md` #9)                                                 | `date-fns` + `@date-fns/tz` (`rules/general.md` #9)                                                  |
| Icons                  | `lucide-react` for functional UI + `react-icons/pi` (Phosphor Duotone) for decorative surfaces only, both encapsulated inside `packages/ui` (`rules/frontend.md` #17) | —                                                                                                    |
| CSRF protection        | Native `Sec-Fetch-Site` / `Origin` browser headers (or Next 16 `src/proxy.ts` BFF `Origin` check)   | Native `app.enableCsrfProtection()` (`csrf-csrf` only via ADR; never `csurf` — `rules/nestjs.md` #20) |
| Slug generation        | `slugify`                                                                                           | `slugify`                                                                                            |
| Styling                | Tailwind v4 utilities only (`rules/frontend.md` #4–#5)                                              | —                                                                                                    |
| UI primitives          | `shadcn/ui` — multi-variant components via `cva` + `cn` (`rules/frontend.md` #8)                    | —                                                                                                    |
| Class merging          | `cn` (`shadcn-ui/cn`) — direct import, no `lib/utils.ts` wrapper                                    | —                                                                                                    |
| i18n                   | `next-intl` on Next.js; `useI18n()` + JSON catalogs on Vite/React & miniapp (`rules/i18n.md`)       | —                                                                                                    |

rules.title: Library baseline: additional concerns
rules.content:
0b. **Library baseline: additional concerns** — Use the applicable baseline in this table.

| Concern                | Web/React (portal, web, mobile-rn)                                                                  | NestJS (`apps/api`)                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Charts                 | `recharts` for static/dashboard draws; `uPlot` for ≥30 Hz streaming feeds                           | —                                                                                                    |
| Animation              | CSS `@keyframes` by default; `motion` (`motion/react`) for stagger, interruptible, or scroll-linked | —                                                                                                    |
| Tests                  | `vitest` (or `bun test --check` in Bun-native repos, `rules/general.md` #18)                        | `vitest` (or `bun test --check` in Bun-native repos)                                                 |
| ORM                    | —                                                                                                   | Prisma 7 — `prisma-client` generator + `@prisma/client` alias (`rules/prisma.md`)                    |
| API docs               | —                                                                                                   | `@nestjs/swagger` plugin with `classValidatorShim: true` (`rules/nestjs.md` #8)                      |
| Authentication         | —                                                                                                   | `@nestjs/authentication` + `@nestjs/authorization`; `@nestjs/jwt` only for a task-fixed token contract ([official auth reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nestjs/agent-skills/master/skills/nestjs-auth/references/authentication.md)) |
| Password hashing       | —                                                                                                   | `@nestjs/authentication` `PasswordHasher` for NestJS sign-in ([official auth reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nestjs/agent-skills/master/skills/nestjs-auth/references/authentication.md)); `argon2` / `Bun.password` only under rule 14 |
| Rate limiting          | —                                                                                                   | `@nestjs/throttler`                                                                                  |
| WebSockets             | —                                                                                                   | `@nestjs/websockets` + `@nestjs/platform-ws` (`WsAdapter`)                                           |
| Security headers       | —                                                                                                   | `helmet`                                                                                             |
| Email (transactional)  | —                                                                                                   | `@nestjs/mail` (`rules/nestjs.md` #22)                                                               |
| File & object storage  | — (uploads ride `axios` `postForm` — `rules/upload.md`)                                             | `@nestjs/storage` (`StorageDisk`: `LocalDisk`, `S3Disk`, `InMemoryDisk` — `rules/upload.md`)         |
| Malware scanning       | —                                                                                                   | `clamscan` (`preference: 'clamdscan'`, ADR-0028 slice only)                                          |

**Miniapp exception**: The Zalo webview miniapp keeps its own `fetch` client (`api/client.ts`) and local UI components (`rules/frontend.md` #11, ADR-0039); table rows apply to it only where stated.

rules.title: One HTTP client per framework (`axios` on web, `@nestjs/http-client` on NestJS)
rules.content: 1. **One HTTP client per framework (`axios` on web, `@nestjs/http-client` on NestJS)** — No `fetch`-wrapper hand-rolls, `got`, `ky`, `undici`, `@nestjs/axios`, or raw `axios` in NestJS. Sole exception: browser SSE/NDJSON streaming endpoints use `fetch` sharing `baseURL` and `authHeader()` (`rules/frontend.md` #11).

rules.title: `zod` + `react-hook-form` (`zodResolver`) on web clients
rules.content: 2. **`zod` + `react-hook-form` (`zodResolver`) on web clients** — No `yup`, `joi`, `io-ts`, `formik`, or manual per-field `useState`. The zod schema is the single source of truth (`z.infer`).

rules.title: `@tanstack/react-query` owns server state
rules.content: 3. **`@tanstack/react-query` owns server state** — No SWR, RTK Query, `useEffect` + `fetch`, or `react-infinite-scroll-*` packages (use `useInfiniteQuery` + `IntersectionObserver`).

rules.title: `class-validator` + `class-transformer` own NestJS request boundaries
rules.content: 4. **`class-validator` + `class-transformer` own NestJS request boundaries** — DTO classes validate `@Body()`/`@Query()`/`@Param()`. `zod` runs in the API **only** for boot-time `ConfigModule.forRoot({ validationSchema })` (`rules/nestjs.md` #18).

rules.title: `date-fns` + `@date-fns/tz` own time handling
rules.content: 5. **`date-fns` + `@date-fns/tz` own time handling** — No `dayjs`, `luxon`, or `moment` (`rules/general.md` #9).

rules.title: Native CSRF check by default; `csrf-csrf` only via ADR
rules.content: 6. **Native CSRF check by default; `csrf-csrf` only via ADR** — Cookie-authenticated NestJS apps use built-in `app.enableCsrfProtection({ trustedOrigins })`; cookie-less APIs behind a Next 16 BFF enforce the `Origin` allowlist in `src/proxy.ts` (`rules/nestjs.md` #20). Never install deprecated `csurf`.

rules.title: Research with Context7, then `webfetch`, before calling a library API
rules.content: 7. **Research with Context7, then `webfetch`, before calling a library API** — Before adding or modifying any library call: (a) use the library assigned by the table above; (b) query Context7 (`resolve-library-id` → `query-docs`) for the exact API and installed version; (c) fall back to official docs via `webfetch` if Context7 lacks coverage. Never write library calls from memory.

rules.title: Shared icon vocabulary in `packages/ui`: `lucide-react` for functional UI, `react-icons/pi` (Duotone) for decorative surfaces
rules.content:
8. **Shared icon vocabulary in `packages/ui`: `lucide-react` for functional UI, `react-icons/pi` (Duotone) for decorative surfaces** —
   - Declare `lucide-react` and `react-icons` in `packages/ui` only; apps never import icon packages directly or hand-roll inline `<svg>` / Unicode glyphs (`✓`, `→`, `▣`, emojis). Miniapp re-exports all icons through `@/components/ui` (barrel over `icons.tsx` / `icons-lucide.tsx`).
   - Export `<Icon icon={ICON.<concept>} size="md" />` (`xs: 12`, `sm: 14`, `md: 16`, `lg: 20`, `xl: 24`, fixed `strokeWidth = 2`, `currentColor`) for all functional UI. Keys in `ICON` name domain concepts (`ICON.classes`, `ICON.tuition`, `ICON.sla`), never shapes or screens.
   - `lucide-react` (2,159 icons) has wider coverage than `react-icons/pi` (1,512 icons); never add `react-icons` for "missing coverage." Restrict `react-icons/pi` (Phosphor Duotone) to `<RichIcon icon={RICH_ICON.<concept>} />` on decorative surfaces (landing heroes, feature cards, empty states), where every `RICH_ICON` key is a subset of `ICON` (Precedent: Gia Su Anh Minh 2026-10, ADR-0008).

rules.title: `slugify` with `{ lower: true, strict: true, locale: "vi" }`
rules.content: 9. **`slugify` with `{ lower: true, strict: true, locale: "vi" }`** — Without `locale: "vi"`, `Đà Nẵng` transliterates to `dja-nang`; `String.normalize("NFD")` also misses `đ`/`Đ`. Never hand-roll slug regexes.

rules.title: `cn` (`shadcn-ui/cn`) is the only class-merge library
rules.content: 10. **`cn` (`shadcn-ui/cn`) is the only class-merge library** — Import `import { cn } from 'cn'` directly (`createCn` from `'cn/config'`). No `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, or `lib/utils.ts` wrapper; set `components.json` `"aliases": { "utils": "cn" }`. Keep `fast-uri >= 3.1.6` in workspace overrides.

rules.title: `@nestjs/throttler` is in-process by default; `WsAdapter` before `socket.io`
rules.content: 11. **`@nestjs/throttler` is in-process by default; `WsAdapter` before `socket.io`** — Record single-instance throttler assumptions in an ADR before dropping Redis rate-limiting (multi-instance multiplies limits, ADR-0020). Run WebSocket gateways on `@nestjs/platform-ws` (`WsAdapter`); use `socket.io` only when a greenfield surface requires rooms/reconnect framing.

rules.title: `uPlot` streams (≥30 FPS), `recharts` draws (static/dashboard)
rules.content: 12. **`uPlot` streams (≥30 FPS), `recharts` draws (static/dashboard)** — Feed both from a bounded ring buffer of the last $N$ samples so streaming data never leaks memory (Precedent: CareAI 2026-10).

rules.title: `@nestjs/mail` owns API email; `@nestjs/storage` owns API file/object storage
rules.content: 13. **`@nestjs/mail` owns API email; `@nestjs/storage` owns API file/object storage** — No `nodemailer`, raw provider HTTP calls, or direct `@aws-sdk/client-s3` in feature modules (`rules/nestjs.md` #22–#23, `rules/upload.md`). Repos still on the legacy `@aws-sdk/client-s3` `StorageService` keep it until migrated in a dedicated PR.

rules.title: `Bun.password` only on Bun-only runtimes, with forced rotation
rules.content: 14. **`Bun.password` only on Bun-only runtimes, with forced rotation** — `Bun.password.hash(value, { algorithm: "argon2id" })` replaces the `argon2` package only where every runtime is Bun: it throws under Node, and it rejects hashes the `argon2` package wrote (`PASSWORD_INVALID_ENCODING`), so rotate all stored hashes in the same change and run production on Bun (Precedent: Gia Su Anh Minh 2026-10 — NestJS API and Next.js standalone verified serving on `oven/bun:1.4.4`, full image builds green). Keep `argon2` everywhere else.

rules.title: `Bun-first`: check latest Bun built-ins before adding a library
rules.content: 15. **`Bun-first`: check latest Bun built-ins before adding a library** — Where every runtime is Bun (`oven/bun:*`, `bun dist/main.js`): check `bun.com/docs/runtime/*` for the current release first. Use the built-in when it covers the concern (`Bun.Image` for resize/convert, `Bun.file`/`Bun.write`, `Bun.s3`, `Bun.redis`, `Bun.SQL`, `Bun.password`). Add a library only when the built-in lacks coverage, and record the check in the PR. Never add `sharp`, `argon2`, `ioredis`, `pg`, or `aws-sdk` for a covered built-in on Bun-only runtimes.

rules.title: `@nestjs/ai` owns NestJS model access; `@ai-sdk/react` owns chat UI
rules.content: 16. **`@nestjs/ai` owns NestJS model access; `@ai-sdk/react` owns chat UI** — Register models in `AiModule` and call `AiService`; feature services never construct `@ai-sdk/*` providers or call the raw SDK (`rules/nestjs-ai.md`). On web clients, `@ai-sdk/react` `useChat` consumes the UI-message stream from the API route. Docs: https://docs.nestjs.com/ai/overview.

# Library Baseline — one library per concern, chosen by framework

<!-- rule: library-baseline-core -->
0a. **Library baseline: core concerns** — Use the applicable baseline in this table.

Applies to every TypeScript/JavaScript project. One library per concern, fixed by framework. A substitute library is a violation, not a preference. Reach for this table first, then verify the chosen library's current API via Rule 7 before writing calls.

## The table

| Concern                | Web/React (portal, web, mobile-rn)                                                                  | NestJS (`apps/api`)                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| HTTP client            | `axios` (`rules/frontend.md` #1, #11)                                                               | `@nestjs/http-client` (`rules/nestjs.md` #21)                                                        |
| Runtime validation     | `zod`                                                                                               | `class-validator` + `class-transformer` (`zod` only for boot `env.schema.ts`, `rules/nestjs.md` #18) |
| Forms                  | `react-hook-form` + `@hookform/resolvers/zod`                                                       | —                                                                                                    |
| Server state           | `@tanstack/react-query`                                                                             | —                                                                                                    |
| AI models, agents      | `@ai-sdk/react` `useChat` for chat UI                                                               | `@nestjs/ai` (`AiModule` + `AiService` + `@AgentFunction` — `rules/nestjs-ai.md`)                    |
| Time                   | `date-fns` + `@date-fns/tz` (`rules/general.md` #9)                                                 | `date-fns` + `@date-fns/tz` (`rules/general.md` #9)                                                  |
| Icons                  | `lucide-react` for functional UI + `react-icons/pi` (Phosphor Duotone) for decorative surfaces only, both encapsulated inside `packages/ui` (`rules/frontend.md` #17) | —                                                                                                    |
| CSRF protection        | Native `Sec-Fetch-Site` / `Origin` browser headers (or Next 16 `src/proxy.ts` BFF `Origin` check)   | Native `app.enableCsrfProtection()` (`csrf-csrf` only via ADR; never `csurf` — `rules/nestjs.md` #20) |
| Slug generation        | `slugify`                                                                                           | `slugify`                                                                                            |
| Styling                | Tailwind v4 utilities only (`rules/frontend.md` #4–#5)                                              | —                                                                                                    |
| UI primitives          | `shadcn/ui` — multi-variant components via `cva` + `cn` (`rules/frontend.md` #8)                    | —                                                                                                    |
| Class merging          | `cn` (`shadcn-ui/cn`) — direct import, no `lib/utils.ts` wrapper                                    | —                                                                                                    |
| i18n                   | `next-intl` on Next.js; `useI18n()` + JSON catalogs on Vite/React & miniapp (`rules/i18n.md`)       | —                                                                                                    |

<!-- rule: library-baseline-other -->
0b. **Library baseline: additional concerns** — Use the applicable baseline in this table.

| Concern                | Web/React (portal, web, mobile-rn)                                                                  | NestJS (`apps/api`)                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Charts                 | `recharts` for static/dashboard draws; `uPlot` for ≥30 Hz streaming feeds                           | —                                                                                                    |
| Animation              | CSS `@keyframes` by default; `motion` (`motion/react`) for stagger, interruptible, or scroll-linked | —                                                                                                    |
| Tests                  | `vitest` (or `bun test --check` in Bun-native repos, `rules/general.md` #18)                        | `vitest` (or `bun test --check` in Bun-native repos)                                                 |
| ORM                    | —                                                                                                   | Prisma 7 — `prisma-client` generator + `@prisma/client` alias (`rules/prisma.md`)                    |
| API docs               | —                                                                                                   | `@nestjs/swagger` plugin with `classValidatorShim: true` (`rules/nestjs.md` #8)                      |
| Authentication         | —                                                                                                   | `@nestjs/authentication` + `@nestjs/authorization`; `@nestjs/jwt` only for a task-fixed token contract ([official auth reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nestjs/agent-skills/master/skills/nestjs-auth/references/authentication.md)) |
| Password hashing       | —                                                                                                   | `@nestjs/authentication` `PasswordHasher` for NestJS sign-in ([official auth reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nestjs/agent-skills/master/skills/nestjs-auth/references/authentication.md)); `argon2` / `Bun.password` only under rule 14 |
| Rate limiting          | —                                                                                                   | `@nestjs/throttler`                                                                                  |
| WebSockets             | —                                                                                                   | `@nestjs/websockets` + `@nestjs/platform-ws` (`WsAdapter`)                                           |
| Security headers       | —                                                                                                   | `helmet`                                                                                             |
| Email (transactional)  | —                                                                                                   | `@nestjs/mail` (`rules/nestjs.md` #22)                                                               |
| File & object storage  | — (uploads ride `axios` `postForm` — `rules/upload.md`)                                             | `@nestjs/storage` (`StorageDisk`: `LocalDisk`, `S3Disk`, `InMemoryDisk` — `rules/upload.md`)         |
| Malware scanning       | —                                                                                                   | `clamscan` (`preference: 'clamdscan'`, ADR-0028 slice only)                                          |

**Miniapp exception**: The Zalo webview miniapp keeps its own `fetch` client (`api/client.ts`) and local UI components (`rules/frontend.md` #11, ADR-0039); table rows apply to it only where stated.

Never write library calls from memory.
<!-- rule: shared-icon-vocabulary-in-pa -->

   - Declare `lucide-react` and `react-icons` in `packages/ui` only; apps never import icon packages directly or hand-roll inline `<svg>` / Unicode glyphs (`✓`, `→`, `▣`, emojis). Miniapp re-exports all icons through `@/components/ui` (barrel over `icons.tsx` / `icons-lucide.tsx`).
   - Export `<Icon icon={ICON.<concept>} size="md" />` (`xs: 12`, `sm: 14`, `md: 16`, `lg: 20`, `xl: 24`, fixed `strokeWidth = 2`, `currentColor`) for all functional UI. Keys in `ICON` name domain concepts (`ICON.classes`, `ICON.tuition`, `ICON.sla`), never shapes or screens.
   - `lucide-react` (2,159 icons) has wider coverage than `react-icons/pi` (1,512 icons); never add `react-icons` for "missing coverage." <!-- rule: slugify-with-lower-true-stri -->

Run WebSocket gateways on `@nestjs/platform-ws` (`WsAdapter`); use `socket.io` only when a greenfield surface requires rooms/reconnect framing.

entries.title: Lint & Format Baseline — bun fmt, bun lint, Ruff (Python)
entries.name: Lint & Format Baseline — bun fmt, bun lint, Ruff (Python)
entries.description: Applies to every TypeScript/JavaScript and Python project in the organization. Machine-readable configs ship in `configs/`.
entries.scope: All TS/JS and Python projects

rules.title: Module context
rules.content:
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to every TypeScript/JavaScript and Python project in the organization. Machine-readable configs ship in `configs/`.

## Scope & tool split

| Tool      | Applies to                                                             | Job             |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `bun fmt` | all TS/JS/Next.js/JSON/YAML/CSS projects (`configs/.oxfmtrc.json`)     | formatting only |
| `bun lint` | all TS/JS and Next.js 16+ projects (`configs/.oxlintrc.json` / `oxlint.config.ts`, read by `bun lint`) | linting only    |
| Ruff      | Python packages (`ruff format` + `ruff check`, plus `mypy` & `pytest`) | format + lint   |

Formatting is never linted; linting is never formatted (zero stylistic rules in any linter).

rules.title: One root `.oxfmtrc.json` read natively by `bun fmt` — no `oxfmt` package, no per-app overrides
rules.content: 1. **One root `.oxfmtrc.json` read natively by `bun fmt` — no `oxfmt` package, no per-app overrides** — Copy `configs/.oxfmtrc.json` (`singleQuote: true`, `sortPackageJson: false`, `ignorePatterns: ["*.md", "**/next-env.d.ts"]`) to the repo root. Run `"format": "bun fmt"` and `"format:check": "bun fmt --check"` across all workspaces (including Next.js apps). Use static `.oxfmtrc.json` rather than `oxfmt.config.ts`: `bun fmt` (Bun 1.4.4+) parses `.oxfmtrc.json` natively in Zig/C++ 3×–6× faster without loading the `oxfmt` JS package, allowing `bun remove oxfmt` (`bun fmt --doctor` verifies 100% native formatting and zero removable packages). If a repo has `oxfmt.config.ts`, serialize its resolved export to `.oxfmtrc.json`, delete `oxfmt.config.ts`, and run `bun remove oxfmt`. Never delete `.oxfmtrc.json` or migrate settings into `bunfig.toml [fmt]` (without `.oxfmtrc.json`, Bun falls back to its own printer and reformats 510/806 files — Precedent: Gia Su Anh Minh 2026-10, ADR-0012). Delete any app-level config (config drift) and reformat from root.

rules.title: Tailwind class sorting
rules.content: 2. **Tailwind class sorting** — Set `"sortTailwindcss": true` in Tailwind projects (built-in, no plugin).

rules.title: Markdown is never auto-formatted
rules.content: 3. **Markdown is never auto-formatted** — `*.md` stays in `ignorePatterns` so hand-wrapped rules, ADRs, and specs are not reflowed.

rules.title: `bun lint --no-script` needs a Bun build that supports it
rules.content: 3a. **`bun lint --no-script` needs a Bun build that supports it** — Bun 1.4.4 stable does not; the canary does. On a build without the flag, `bun lint` runs the package `lint` script and appends its arguments. A script named `lint` that calls `bun lint` then re-runs itself until `E2BIG`, exits `0`, and turbo caches the result as a success. Assert the flag in CI from a directory without a `package.json`: `(cd "$(mktemp -d)" && bun lint --help | grep -q -- --no-script)`. Pin a canary build at a separate path when needed; never trust the local Bun version (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — every lint job cancelled for a week, 401 MB job log).

rules.title: Root config (`configs/.oxlintrc.json` or Ultracite `oxlint.config.ts`)
rules.content:
4. **Root config (`configs/.oxlintrc.json` or Ultracite `oxlint.config.ts`)** —
   - `categories`: `correctness: "error"`, `suspicious: "warn"`, `perf: "warn"`.
   - `plugins`: `["react", "react_perf", "nextjs", "typescript", "import", "jest", "vitest"]`.
   - `ignorePatterns`: `node_modules/**`, `dist/**`, `.next/**`, `coverage/**`, `.turbo/**`, `build/**`, `www/**`, `test-results/**`, `.expo/**`, `**/next-env.d.ts`.

rules.title: No type-aware linting
rules.content: 5. **No type-aware linting** — Keep `typeAware`/`typeCheck` off so lint stays a fast save-time pass; semantic type checking belongs to `tsc` / `bun check`.

rules.title: `_`-prefix convention (never a silencer for real input)
rules.content: 6. **`_`-prefix convention (never a silencer for real input)** — `no-unused-vars: ["error", { varsIgnorePattern: "^_", argsIgnorePattern: "^_", caughtErrorsIgnorePattern: "^_" }]`. Prefixing a real input (a DTO, route param, or state setter) with `_` to silence lint is a **suppressed binding** bug — wire it or remove it. Valid `_` uses are signature-required placeholders only (guard params, `validate(_value, args)`, react-query `(_data, ...)`, test stubs).

rules.title: Discipline rules & NestJS decorator allowance
rules.content: 7. **Discipline rules & NestJS decorator allowance** — `no-console: ["warn", { "allow": ["warn", "error"] }]`, `no-debugger: "warn"`, `no-explicit-any: "error"`, `eslint/no-underscore-dangle: "off"`, `react/no-array-index-key: "warn"`, `react/react-in-jsx-scope: "off"`, `import/no-duplicates: ["error", { "prefer-inline": true }]`, `import/no-named-as-default-member: "off"`, `import/no-unassigned-import: "off"`. NestJS repos add `typescript/no-extraneous-class: ["warn", { "allowWithDecorator": true }]`.

rules.title: Scoped test leniency
rules.content: 8. **Scoped test leniency** — Only `**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,tsx}` overrides disable `no-explicit-any`, `expect-expect`, `no-conditional-expect`, `valid-title`, and `require-mock-type-parameters`. App code never inherits test leniency.

rules.title: 300-line cap (`max-lines: ["error", 300]`) — always run `bun fmt` BEFORE the linter
rules.content: 9. **300-line cap (`max-lines: ["error", 300]`) — always run `bun fmt` BEFORE the linter** — `bun fmt` expands compact single-line JSX props, objects, and destructuring by **1.4×–2.5×**. Running the linter before the formatter gives a false-green that fails at commit time under `lint-staged`. Always run the formatter first (`bun fmt <paths> && bun lint --no-script --max-warnings=0 --allow-unsupported <paths>`). Target **≤250 formatted lines** when authoring new components and **≤290 formatted lines** on near-cap edits (Precedent: Gia Su Anh Minh 2026-10 — 65 subagent files expanded past 300 lines on formatting).

rules.title: The CI format gate runs before lint, as its own step or job
rules.content: 9a. **The CI format gate runs before lint, as its own step or job** — A lint failure must not hide formatting debt. Authors run `bun fmt` then `bun lint`; CI runs `format:check` before `lint` (or in a parallel job), so both results are visible in one run. Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — 37 unformatted files on `main` stayed hidden while the lint step failed.

rules.title: Resolve findings in code or config `overrides`, never inline disable comments
rules.content: 10. **Resolve findings in code or config `overrides`, never inline disable comments** — Baseline `bun lint` ignores inline comments (`eslint-disable-next-line`, `oxlint-ignore-next-line`, `oxlint-disable-next-line`), so inline comments are dead code wearing a disguise. Fix the code, or place legitimate framework/target carve-outs in a scoped `overrides` block in config with a comment explaining why. Grep for `disable-next-line|oxlint-ignore` before claiming zero findings.

rules.title: Root `bun lint --no-script --allow-unsupported` (`plugins: ["nextjs"]`) + `bun fmt` by default
rules.content: 11. **Root `bun lint --no-script --allow-unsupported` (`plugins: ["nextjs"]`) + `bun fmt` by default** — Next.js 16+ repos lint all workspaces with root `bun lint --no-script --max-warnings=0 --allow-unsupported` (`plugins: ["nextjs"]` in `.oxlintrc.json` or `oxlint.config.ts`, ADR-0002/0012) and format with `bun fmt`, forbidding per-app ESLint/Prettier configs. Repos still on per-app `eslint.config.mjs`: port the rules to scoped `overrides` (keep `// ponytail:` trigger comments), delete `apps/<app>/eslint.config.mjs`, drop `eslint*` devDeps (Precedent: VibeHost 2026-10 — root `bun lint --no-script --max-warnings=0 --allow-unsupported` lints all six Next.js apps clean).

rules.title: `react-hooks` rules stay ON
rules.content: 12. **`react-hooks` rules stay ON** — Keep `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, `react-hooks/immutability`, and `react-hooks/refs` enabled; disable per-project only with a `// ponytail:` trigger comment after confirming a genuine pervasive conflict.

rules.title: `lint-staged` carries lint-fix tasks only — the formatter runs exactly once, after it
rules.content:
13. **`lint-staged` carries lint-fix tasks only — the formatter runs exactly once, after it** — Keep `bun lint --no-script --fix --allow-unsupported` in `lint-staged`. Never list the formatter there when the hook also runs `bun fmt --staged`: one `--staged` run formats every staged file idempotently, a second run only slows the hook (Precedent: VibeHost 2026-10 — `bun fmt` in `lint-staged` duplicated hook-level `bun fmt --staged`). Fix-then-format: `--fix` mutates code, so a fix applied after formatting can leave unformatted code that nothing later catches (formatting is never linted). Hook shape:
    ```sh
    bunx lint-staged   # bun lint --no-script --fix --allow-unsupported only — no formatter entry
    bun fmt --staged   # single format pass, re-stages
    bun run lint
    bun run typecheck
    ```
    - Scope workspace-owned formatters to their workspace and swallow appended file args: `"*.prisma": "bash -c 'pnpm --filter @acme/api exec prisma format' --"`.

rules.title: Pre-commit runs lint-staged → fmt → full `lint` → `typecheck`; full `test` stays in CI
rules.content: 13b. **Pre-commit runs lint-staged → fmt → full `lint` → `typecheck`; full `test` stays in CI** — The hook must be deterministic and DB-free: staged fix first, then `bun fmt --staged` (formats and re-stages — the committed shape), then the repo's own gates (`lint:boundaries` plus custom checks — not just the linter binary CI also runs) on that final shape so `max-lines` is enforced after `bun fmt` expansion, then typecheck. Keep the full test suite in CI, where the database is guaranteed: a DB-dependent hook red-bars behavior-untouched commits on a cold cache (Precedent: Gia Su Anh Minh 2026-10 — hook ~5s with `lint` 3.4s cold and `typecheck` 1.3s cached; `test` runs in the CI `test` + `verify` jobs).

rules.title: Orphan-export check after symbol swaps
rules.content: 14. **Orphan-export check after symbol swaps** — No linter flags unused `export` bindings. Whenever an edit removes the last reference to an exported constant, type, or helper, grep the repo for its name and delete the orphan definition in the same commit.

rules.title: Mechanical guards
rules.content:
14a. **Mechanical guards** — Run these guards outside the linter:

The linter cannot see a pass-through alias, an inline suppression, or a stale generated file. Add these checks to the repo's `lint` script (or a pre-commit step) and run them on changed files:

- **Pass-through re-exports** — fail on `export { X as Y } from '...'` outside a package entrypoint or an intentional public barrel. The fix is to update every in-repo caller, not to preserve the old name (`rules/general.md` #13). Command shape: `rg -nE "export \{[^}]* as [^}]*\} from" <changed files>` with the entrypoint allowlist.
- **Inline suppressions** — fail on any new `eslint-disable`, `oxlint-disable`, `oxlint-ignore`, or `@ts-ignore` in changed source. Resolve the finding, or put a scoped config override with a reason (`rules/linting.md` #10). Command shape: `rg -nE "(eslint|oxlint|ts)-(disable|ignore)" <changed files>`.
- **Type-bypass casts** — review every new `as never` or `as unknown as` in non-test source. They are allowed only at an adapter boundary that the type system cannot express; the cast gets a comment naming the boundary. A cast used to silence a mismatch is a bug.
- **Generated files stay current** — every `*:generate` script has a matching `*:check` that rewrites to a temp file or compares content, and the root `lint`/CI runs `check`. A generated file without a check is a cache that will drift.

Run the guards after `bun fmt`, because formatting changes line numbers. The gate is green only when the commands return no unallowlisted hit.

rules.title: One root `ruff.toml`: `ruff format` + `ruff check` + `mypy` + `pytest`
rules.content: 15. **One root `ruff.toml`: `ruff format` + `ruff check` + `mypy` + `pytest`** — Select `E`, `F`, `I`, `UP`, `B`, `SIM`, `PTH`, `RUF` and ignore `E501`. Disable `RUF001`–`RUF003` in `ruff.toml` for projects carrying Vietnamese copy or mathematical symbols (en-dash `–`, `×`, `−`, Greek letters θ/α). Never create per-package `ruff.toml` files.

rules.title: Slop-name and package gates
rules.content:
15a. **Slop-name and package gates** — Apply these checks:

- **Short identifiers**: single-letter bindings are allowed only from the established set `u/r/k/e/s/w/d/n/o` (user, request, key, event, slot/session, withdrawal, day, count). Two-letter abbreviations (`cf`, `ae`, `wb`, ...) are not allowed unless listed in the repo's ADR-0028 §3 exception list. Enforce with an `id-length` rule (min 2) plus the allowlist, so new slop is caught at commit time rather than in a follow-up rename pass. Precedent: giasuanhminh refactor 2026-10.
- **Package gate**: for any package with tests, the gate is `bun test --check` (type-checks the test files and everything they import) before `bun test`. Run it in CI and locally.

rules.title: Type-only imports
rules.content:
15b. **Type-only imports** — Apply this import rule:

- **Type-only imports on their own line** — `import type { X } from "..."`, never `import { type X }`. The inline form leaves a side-effect import at runtime. Enforce with `typescript(no-import-type-side-effects)` (already in oxlint). Precedent: VibeHost 2026-10.

# Lint & Format Baseline — bun fmt, bun lint, Ruff (Python)

<!-- rule: module-context -->
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to every TypeScript/JavaScript and Python project in the organization. Machine-readable configs ship in `configs/`.

## Scope & tool split

| Tool      | Applies to                                                             | Job             |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `bun fmt` | all TS/JS/Next.js/JSON/YAML/CSS projects (`configs/.oxfmtrc.json`)     | formatting only |
| `bun lint` | all TS/JS and Next.js 16+ projects (`configs/.oxlintrc.json` / `oxlint.config.ts`, read by `bun lint`) | linting only    |
| Ruff      | Python packages (`ruff format` + `ruff check`, plus `mypy` & `pytest`) | format + lint   |

Formatting is never linted; linting is never formatted (zero stylistic rules in any linter).

## `bun fmt` baseline (all projects, including Next.js)

<!-- rule: one-root-oxfmtrcjson-read-na -->
1. **One root `.oxfmtrc.json` read natively by `bun fmt` — no `oxfmt` package, no per-app overrides** — Copy `configs/.oxfmtrc.json` (`singleQuote: true`, `sortPackageJson: false`, `ignorePatterns: ["*.md", "**/next-env.d.ts"]`) to the repo root. Run `"format": "bun fmt"` and `"format:check": "bun fmt --check"` across all workspaces (including Next.js apps). Use static `.oxfmtrc.json` rather than `oxfmt.config.ts`: `bun fmt` (Bun 1.4.4+) parses `.oxfmtrc.json` natively in Zig/C++ 3×–6× faster without loading the `oxfmt` JS package, allowing `bun remove oxfmt` (`bun fmt --doctor` verifies 100% native formatting and zero removable packages). If a repo has `oxfmt.config.ts`, serialize its resolved export to `.oxfmtrc.json`, delete `oxfmt.config.ts`, and run `bun remove oxfmt`. Never delete `.oxfmtrc.json` or migrate settings into `bunfig.toml [fmt]` (without `.oxfmtrc.json`, Bun falls back to its own printer and reformats 510/806 files — Precedent: Gia Su Anh Minh 2026-10, ADR-0012). Delete any app-level config (config drift) and reformat from root.
<!-- rule: tailwind-class-sorting -->
2. **Tailwind class sorting** — Set `"sortTailwindcss": true` in Tailwind projects (built-in, no plugin).
<!-- rule: markdown-is-never-auto-forma -->
3. **Markdown is never auto-formatted** — `*.md` stays in `ignorePatterns` so hand-wrapped rules, ADRs, and specs are not reflowed.

## Python baseline

<!-- rule: one-root-rufftoml-ruff-forma -->
15. **One root `ruff.toml`: `ruff format` + `ruff check` + `mypy` + `pytest`** — Select `E`, `F`, `I`, `UP`, `B`, `SIM`, `PTH`, `RUF` and ignore `E501`. entries.title: Miniapp Rules — Zalo Mini App
entries.name: Miniapp Rules — Zalo Mini App
entries.description: Applies to Zalo Mini App clients (`zmp-ui` / ZMP, `apps/miniapp` shape). Browser-client baselines live in `rules/frontend.md`; repos with message catalogs additionally include `rules/i18n.md`.
entries.scope: Zalo Mini App (`apps/miniapp`)

rules.title: Module context
rules.content:
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to Zalo Mini App clients (`zmp-ui` / ZMP, `apps/miniapp` shape). Browser-client baselines live in `rules/frontend.md`; repos with message catalogs additionally include `rules/i18n.md`.

rules.title: One left action group per header row: back first, title second, no lone far-right action
rules.content: 1. **One left action group per header row: back first, title second, no lone far-right action** — All icon buttons on a header row form a single group on the left: the back button leftmost, every other action (calendar, bookmark, bell, share) directly right of it, then the title in the remaining space (`flex-1`). A lone action button on the far right is a layout error: it drifts from the back button and risks the host capsule. The same grouping applies to overlay headers on gallery/hero art. Use the shared header primitive's beside-back slot (`afterBack`), never the right slot, for row actions (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — court-list calendar, court-gallery bookmark, tournament-list bell each moved left).

rules.title: Capsule inset comes only from the host variables
rules.content: 2. **Capsule inset comes only from the host variables** — The top inset is `var(--statusbar-h)` and nothing else (no spacer blocks). The horizontal capsule reservation is `var(--capsule-gutter)` on the top row itself, never on the wrapping container (a container padding also shortens full-width content below the row). Drop the reservation when no control reaches the right edge (`right-[18px]`); keep it when the title does.

rules.title: Empty numeric summaries render an explicit zero, never a bare dash
rules.content: 3. **Empty numeric summaries render an explicit zero, never a bare dash** — A `0`-valued total (estimate before selection, empty count) displays `0đ`, not `—`; a dash reads as missing data (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — detail footer estimate).

rules.title: Persist sessions through device storage, never Web Storage directly
rules.content: 4. **Persist sessions through device storage, never Web Storage directly** — The Zalo webview has no `sessionStorage`. A storage abstraction writes to the host SDK's native store on-device and to a `localStorage`-equivalent on web; session code touches only the abstraction (Precedent: Ecopick `device-storage` / `ep_session`).

rules.title: No URL navigation: ZMP keeps a memory router
rules.content: 5. **No URL navigation: ZMP keeps a memory router** — Screens change via store `push`/`go`, never `page.goto`. Deep links are read once from `window.location` at boot through a `PUBLIC_SCREENS` allowlist; state-changing screens stay unreachable by link. Validate every param the allowlist admits.

rules.title: Mock login must not break session restore
rules.content: 6. **Mock login must not break session restore** — A mock-mode flag that short-circuits `restoreSession()` silently breaks token-injection testing. Keep the mock at the login UI, never on the restore path (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — `VITE_ZALO_MOCK=true` broke every `localStorage` session injection in e2e).

rules.title: Every i18n key must render text in both locales
rules.content: 7. **Every i18n key must render text in both locales** — A raw key on screen is a bug: verify label lookups against the real catalog keys (no guessed prefixes) and scan the rendered page in VI and EN after any catalog change (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-08 — `miniapp.` prefix rendered raw keys in quick actions).

rules.title: Screenshot the real component over mocked routes
rules.content: 8. **Screenshot the real component over mocked routes** — Serve the `zmp` dev server, intercept API routes with `**` globs (`*` does not cross `/`), fulfill CORS headers on every mock including `OPTIONS`, drive in-app navigation by tapping (the app renders inside an iframe on a different port), and hide the simulator chrome before capture (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — court/tournament header shots).

rules.title: QA a miniapp at phone width only
rules.content: 9. **QA a miniapp at phone width only** — Capture and review every miniapp screen at `360x760` and `430x932`. Use these two sizes for screenshots, the coverage matrix in `rules/real-user-qa.md`, and the visual audit. Anti-pattern: a `768px` or `1280px` row for a miniapp. A wide sweep hides the capsule gutter and the header inset (rules #2 and #8). If a QA harness owns device profiles, set its miniapp profiles to these two sizes before the sweep (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — capsule gutter and header actions are phone-width concerns; rules #2 and #8).

# Miniapp Rules — Zalo Mini App

<!-- rule: module-context -->
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to Zalo Mini App clients (`zmp-ui` / ZMP, `apps/miniapp` shape). Browser-client baselines live in `rules/frontend.md`; repos with message catalogs additionally include `rules/i18n.md`.

## Capsule zone & header actions (mandatory)

<!-- rule: one-left-action-group-per-he -->
1. **One left action group per header row: back first, title second, no lone far-right action** — All icon buttons on a header row form a single group on the left: the back button leftmost, every other action (calendar, bookmark, bell, share) directly right of it, then the title in the remaining space (`flex-1`). A lone action button on the far right is a layout error: it drifts from the back button and risks the host capsule. The same grouping applies to overlay headers on gallery/hero art. Use the shared header primitive's beside-back slot (`afterBack`), never the right slot, for row actions (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — court-list calendar, court-gallery bookmark, tournament-list bell each moved left).
<!-- rule: capsule-inset-comes-only-fro -->
2. **Capsule inset comes only from the host variables** — The top inset is `var(--statusbar-h)` and nothing else (no spacer blocks). The horizontal capsule reservation is `var(--capsule-gutter)` on the top row itself, never on the wrapping container (a container padding also shortens full-width content below the row). Drop the reservation when no control reaches the right edge (`right-[18px]`); keep it when the title does.
<!-- rule: empty-numeric-summaries-rend -->
3. **Empty numeric summaries render an explicit zero, never a bare dash** — A `0`-valued total (estimate before selection, empty count) displays `0đ`, not `—`; a dash reads as missing data (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — detail footer estimate).

## Zalo host constraints (mandatory)

<!-- rule: persist-sessions-through-dev -->
4. **Persist sessions through device storage, never Web Storage directly** — The Zalo webview has no `sessionStorage`. A storage abstraction writes to the host SDK's native store on-device and to a `localStorage`-equivalent on web; session code touches only the abstraction (Precedent: Ecopick `device-storage` / `ep_session`).
<!-- rule: no-url-navigation-zmp-keeps -->
5. **No URL navigation: ZMP keeps a memory router** — Screens change via store `push`/`go`, never `page.goto`. Deep links are read once from `window.location` at boot through a `PUBLIC_SCREENS` allowlist; state-changing screens stay unreachable by link. Validate every param the allowlist admits.
<!-- rule: mock-login-must-not-break-se -->
6. **Mock login must not break session restore** — A mock-mode flag that short-circuits `restoreSession()` silently breaks token-injection testing. Keep the mock at the login UI, never on the restore path (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — `VITE_ZALO_MOCK=true` broke every `localStorage` session injection in e2e).

## Copy & verification (mandatory)

<!-- rule: every-i18n-key-must-render-t -->
7. **Every i18n key must render text in both locales** — A raw key on screen is a bug: verify label lookups against the real catalog keys (no guessed prefixes) and scan the rendered page in VI and EN after any catalog change (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-08 — `miniapp.` prefix rendered raw keys in quick actions).
<!-- rule: screenshot-the-real-componen -->
8. **Screenshot the real component over mocked routes** — Serve the `zmp` dev server, intercept API routes with `**` globs (`*` does not cross `/`), fulfill CORS headers on every mock including `OPTIONS`, drive in-app navigation by tapping (the app renders inside an iframe on a different port), and hide the simulator chrome before capture (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — court/tournament header shots).
<!-- rule: qa-a-miniapp-at-phone-width -->
9. **QA a miniapp at phone width only** — Capture and review every miniapp screen at `360x760` and `430x932`. Use these two sizes for screenshots, the coverage matrix in `rules/real-user-qa.md`, and the visual audit. Anti-pattern: a `768px` or `1280px` row for a miniapp. A wide sweep hides the capsule gutter and the header inset (rules #2 and #8). If a QA harness owns device profiles, set its miniapp profiles to these two sizes before the sweep (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — capsule gutter and header actions are phone-width concerns; rules #2 and #8).

> **Docs (read before a submission)**: [primary: Apple App Review Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/) · [primary: Google Play policy center](https://play.google/developer-content-policy/) · [playbook: pre-submission checklist](https://mjmirza.github.io/app-store-compliance/PRE-SUBMISSION-CHECKLIST.html) · [playbook: Apple rejection map](https://mjmirza.github.io/app-store-compliance/APPLE.html) · [playbook: Google Play rejection map](https://mjmirza.github.io/app-store-compliance/GOOGLE-PLAY.html) · [playbook: appeal playbook](https://mjmirza.github.io/app-store-compliance/MISTAKE-PATTERNS.html) · [playbook: privacy guide](https://mjmirza.github.io/app-store-compliance/MOBILE-PRIVACY-MONITOR-2026.html) · [playbook: by app type](https://mjmirza.github.io/app-store-compliance/BY-APP-TYPE.html). The playbook is a secondary source. It is not affiliated with Apple or Google. It uses the OpenRoots Agent License 2.3, a non-OSI license. Cite the playbook. Copy no text from it into repo files.

rules.title: Complete the checklist for each target store
rules.content: 1. **Complete the checklist for each target store** — Read the playbook pre-submission checklist before each store submission. Use the Apple section for iOS. Use the Google Play section for Android. Record the result.

rules.title: Do not submit with an open failure
rules.content: 2. **Do not submit with an open failure** — Fix every failed checklist item before you upload the build. Do not submit while a known failure is open.

rules.title: Map each rejection to one guideline and one fix
rules.content: 3. **Map each rejection to one guideline and one fix** — When a store rejects a build, record the exact store guideline, the trigger, and the fix. Use the Apple or Google Play rejection map for the first pass. Use the appeal playbook when you contest the decision.

rules.title: Primary sources govern every rule claim
rules.content: 4. **Primary sources govern every rule claim** — Use the Apple App Review Guidelines and the Google Play policy center for any statement about a store rule. Use the playbook only as a practitioner aid. When the two source types disagree, follow the store source.

entries.name: NestJS AI Rules — `@nestjs/ai` for models, agents and embeddings
entries.description: Applies to NestJS services that call a language model, embed text, or expose tools to a model. Include this file only for those apps; `rules/nestjs.md` covers the rest of the API.
entries.scope: NestJS services with AI features (`@nestjs/ai` models, agents, embeddings)

rules.title: Module context
rules.content:
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to NestJS services that call a language model, embed text, or expose tools to a model. Include this file only for those apps; `rules/nestjs.md` covers the rest of the API.

> **Docs (read before writing calls)**: [overview](https://docs.nestjs.com/ai/overview) · [models](https://docs.nestjs.com/ai/models) · [tools](https://docs.nestjs.com/ai/tools) · [agents](https://docs.nestjs.com/ai/agents) · [embeddings](https://docs.nestjs.com/ai/embeddings) · [testing](https://docs.nestjs.com/ai/testing). Token-lean raw markdown: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nestjs/docs.nestjs.com/master/content/ai/{overview,models,tools,agents,embeddings,testing}.md`. Use Context7 first per `rules/libraries.md` #7.

rules.title: `@nestjs/ai` owns the provider and every model call
rules.content:
1. **`@nestjs/ai` owns the provider and every model call** — Register named models and embedding models once in `AiModule.forRoot()` / `forRootAsync()`, then call them through `AiService` (`generateText`, `generateObject`, `streamText`, `embed`, `embedMany`). Construct `@ai-sdk/*` providers only in the module factory, from `ConfigService`.
   - Feature services do not import `generateText`, `streamText` or `embed` from `ai`, and do not call `createOpenAICompatible` or another provider factory. Keep one model registry, not one client per service.
   - `@InjectModel()` / `@InjectEmbeddingModel()` is the raw-SDK escape hatch. It drops `AiService` timeouts, retries, fallback, budgets and usage events; use it only when the call needs the SDK directly. `AiTools.select()` keeps agent-function schemas, scopes and enhancers for a raw call.

rules.title: Pin the package pair, then prove a clean install
rules.content: 2. **Pin the package pair, then prove a clean install** — `@nestjs/ai` and its `@nestjs/resilience` peer are pre-1.0: pin exact versions and match the `ai` major the package declares (`ai` 7 for `@nestjs/ai` 0.0.x). Run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` after adding them; a package present only in `node_modules` is missing in production.

rules.title: Structured output is a schema, not a prompt
rules.content: 3. **Structured output is a schema, not a prompt** — Use `generateObject()` with a Zod schema and `.describe()` on every field. `AiOutputError` means the answer did not match; do not parse JSON by hand. A plain-text fallback is an application decision: keep it in one service and remember the endpoint's refusal for the process.

rules.title: A model-callable method is a provider method with `@AgentFunction()`
rules.content: 4. **A model-callable method is a provider method with `@AgentFunction()`** — Give it a `name`, a `description` and an object `inputSchema`; list it by name or provider class in the call's `tools`. Do not hand-roll a tool schema, a dispatch loop or a second authorization path.

rules.title: Pass `caller`, declare `scopes`
rules.content: 5. **Pass `caller`, declare `scopes`** — `caller: { request }` in a route; `caller: { user, scopes }` in a queue job. A method with `scopes` runs only when the caller holds them. Guards, interceptors, pipes and filters run with context type `'ai'`; a shared enhancer checks `context.getType()` before `switchToHttp()`.

rules.title: Use `@nestjs/ai/workflows` only for durable or approved runs
rules.content: 6. **Use `@nestjs/ai/workflows` only for durable or approved runs** — A run that waits for a person or survives a restart stores `caller` as `user`/`scopes`; its providers are `@Public()`. Pass `ctx.idempotencyKey` to every side effect. A request/response chat does not need a workflow.

rules.title: Stream through `AiTextStream`
rules.content: 7. **Stream through `AiTextStream`** — `streamText()` exposes `toUIMessageStream()`, `pipeUIMessageStreamToResponse()`, `text`, `usage` and `steps`. Use `pipeUIMessageStreamToResponse()` when the route writes directly; use `toUIMessageStream()` only when the app must mirror chunks (resumable SSE). Feature services do not pipe the raw `ai` SDK stream.

rules.title: Record usage once, in the AI seam
rules.content: 8. **Record usage once, in the AI seam** — Set `onUsage` / `onEmbeddingUsage` on the module or the one wrapper service for tokens, cost and latency; call sites do not duplicate counters. `pricing` is per million tokens; a model without it reports no cost.

rules.title: Embeddings have no fallback
rules.content: 9. **Embeddings have no fallback** — `embed()` / `embedMany()` use the `embeddingModels` registry. Never compare vectors from two models; changing the model or dimensions requires a re-index. Store vectors in `pgvector` or a vector database.

rules.title: No provider in tests
rules.content: 10. **No provider in tests** — Use `FakeModel`, `FakeEmbeddingModel`, `overrideModels()`, `overrideEmbeddingModels()` and `callTool()` from `@nestjs/ai/testing`. Register a real `AiModule.forRoot()` with fakes so retries, timeouts, schemas, agent functions and streaming run as in production. Keep one success-path test for the pipeline; a mocked SDK call proves only the mock.

rules.title: A standalone script imports `reflect-metadata` first
rules.content: 11. **A standalone script imports `reflect-metadata` first** — `@nestjs/ai` is ESM-only; Bun and Node 22+ load it from the CommonJS build. A script that boots `NestFactory.createApplicationContext()` imports `reflect-metadata` before the decorated modules. The normal `main.ts` gets it from `@nestjs/core`.

rules.content:
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to `apps/api`-style NestJS services in the organization. Include this file only for NestJS repos.

> **Pointers**: Time handling (`date-fns` + `TZDate` in `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`) follows `rules/general.md` (#9). File upload & media lifecycle rules live in `rules/upload.md`. Full Prisma 7 setup lives in `rules/prisma.md`. AI models, agent functions and embeddings follow `rules/nestjs-ai.md`.

> **NestJS authority**: the official [nestjs/agent-skills](https://github.com/nestjs/agent-skills) on branch `master` owns current Nest APIs and first-party packages.
