rules.title: DTO class for every `@Body()` and multi-value `@Query()`/`@Param()`
rules.content: 1. **DTO class for every `@Body()` and multi-value `@Query()`/`@Param()`** — Validate at the pipe with `class-validator` decorators on a class, never inside services/controllers. Inline/mapped/intersection types (`{ x: string }`, `Omit<Dto, K>`, `Record<string, unknown>`, `BaseDto & { x: T }`) erase `metatype` to `Object` and **bypass `ValidationPipe`**; use `class ChildDto extends BaseDto` instead. NestJS 12 `schema` (`StandardSchemaValidationPipe`) stays opt-in — keep `class-validator` DTO classes as the default.

rules.title: Route params ride a single `@Param() params: XParamsDto`
rules.content: 2. **Route params ride a single `@Param() params: XParamsDto`** — Never repeat `@Param('storeId') storeId: string, @Param('departmentId') ...`. Decorate every property (whitelist strips undecorated props), compose depth via `extends` (`StoreDepartmentParamsDto extends StoreParamsDto`), put shared shapes in `common/dto/route-params.dto.ts`, and pass `params` intact to the service (Precedent: RestoSuite 2026-08).

rules.title: `whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true` 422s on undeclared fields
rules.content: 3. **`whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true` 422s on undeclared fields** — Confirm the DTO declares any new client query/body param before sending it, and grep every caller before removing a DTO field; swallowed 422s look like blank UI sections (Precedent: XaDaoXa 2026-08).

rules.title: Prisma `DateTime` columns require `@Type(() => Date) @IsDate()`, never `@IsDateString()`
rules.content: 4. **Prisma `DateTime` columns require `@Type(() => Date) @IsDate()`, never `@IsDateString()`** — `@IsDateString()` accepts bare `"2026-08-15"` strings (e.g. from `<input type="date">`), which Prisma `DateTime` rejects at write time with an unhandled 500. `@Type(() => Date) @IsDate()` coerces both date-only and ISO strings into a `Date` at the pipe (Precedent: XaDaoXa 2026-08).

rules.title: Normalization & cross-field rules live in the DTO
rules.content: 5. **Normalization & cross-field rules live in the DTO** — Keep `.toUpperCase()`, CSV splits, `@Type(() => Number)`, and wire-to-DB enum maps in `@Transform`/`@Type` so services receive DB-ready shapes. Implement cross-field checks via `@ValidatorConstraint` + `@Validate(Constraint, [otherField])` in `common/validators/`, conditional requiredness via `@ValidateIf`, custom messages via decorator `{ message }`, and filter enums via `@IsIn([...Object.values(Enum), 'all'])` (400 at pipe, never silently dropped).

rules.title: DTOs pass intact across the controller→service seam
rules.content: 6. **DTOs pass intact across the controller→service seam** — Call `service.method(dto)` (imported with `import type`) without destructuring fields in the controller. Service→service calls and transport composites (cookies + body) may pass primitives.

rules.title: Register literal routes before `:param` routes on the same base
rules.content: 7. **Register literal routes before `:param` routes on the same base** — `GET /things/:id` declared before `GET /things/summary` swallows `"summary"` as `:id`. This applies both to method order inside one controller and to `@Module` import order when two controllers share a `@Controller('prefix')` base. Audit shared prefixes with `grep -hoE "@Controller\('[^']+'\)" src -r | sort | uniq -d` (Precedent: XaDaoXa 2026-08).

rules.title: No `@ApiProperty` when `classValidatorShim: true` is enabled
rules.content: 8. **No `@ApiProperty` when `classValidatorShim: true` is enabled** — With `@nestjs/swagger` plugin (`classValidatorShim: true`, `introspectComments: true`) in `nest-cli.json`, types/requiredness/enums come from `class-validator` and examples/descriptions come from JSDoc (`/** example: Sân Tao Đàn */`). Never duplicate `@ApiProperty`/`@ApiPropertyOptional` (Precedent: ponytail audit 2026-08, 634 decorators removed).

rules.title: Folder per file type when count ≥ 2
rules.content:
9. **Folder per file type when count ≥ 2** — A file type appearing **2+ times** in a module lives in a plural folder (`services/`, `controllers/`, `schedulers/`, `policies/`, `guards/`, `decorators/`, `strategies/`, `mappers/`, `testing/`, plus `dto/`, `repo/`, `middleware/`); a lone file of its type stays at the module root:
   - **Strict membership & root vocabulary**: type folders hold only that type. `<module>.types.ts`, `<module>.errors.ts`, `<module>.http.ts`, `<module>.mapper.ts`, `<module>.module.ts`, `index.ts`, and unsuffixed files (`permissions.ts`) stay at the module root. When a service or repo approaches `max-lines: 300` or `complexity: 20` due to Prisma create/update normalization or response row mapping, extract a pure `<module>.mapper.ts` at the module root (move to `mappers/` when count ≥ 2).
   - **Spec placement**: unit `*.spec.ts` files sit beside the file they test (`services/foo.service.spec.ts`); module-booting `*.integration.spec.ts`, `*.e2e.spec.ts`, and `*.http.spec.ts` stay at the module root; 2+ `*.spec-setup.ts` / `*-mock.ts` files move to `testing/`.
   - **No barrel in type folders**: `module/index.ts` is the only surface; enforce layout counts via a lint script and migrate existing modules only in dedicated compliance commits (Precedent: VibeHost ADR-0024).

rules.title: Split request DTOs from response/shared types
rules.content: 10. **Split request DTOs from response/shared types** — Request contracts live in `module_name/dto/*.dto.ts`; response shapes, pagination wrappers, and cross-module row types live in `module_name/<module>.types.ts`.

rules.title: Relative-when-shorter imports
rules.content: 11. **Relative-when-shorter imports** — Import across folders via `@/<folder>/...` unless the relative path (`../dto/create-video.dto`) is shorter; import defining files directly and keep same-folder imports relative.

rules.title: Import `@Global()` infra modules once in `AppModule`
rules.content: 12. **Import `@Global()` infra modules once in `AppModule`** — Never re-import `PrismaInfraModule`, `ClsModule`, or `ConfigModule` in child modules.

rules.title: Break `X → Y → X` module cycles with a neutral `*CoreModule`
rules.content: 13. **Break `X → Y → X` module cycles with a neutral `*CoreModule`** — Extract dependency-free providers into `*CoreModule` imported by both sides; never re-register foreign `{ provide: TOKEN, useClass }` bindings or reach for `forwardRef()` (Precedent: TaxEasy 2026-08).

rules.title: Flat domain-verb repos (`module_name/repo/<name>.repo.ts`), class is the contract
rules.content: 14. **Flat domain-verb repos (`module_name/repo/<name>.repo.ts`), class is the contract** — Services never inject `PrismaService` directly. Each repo class (`<Entity>Repo` — no `Prisma` prefix, no `Repository` suffix, no `I*Repository` interface, no `repo/index.ts` barrel, no `*.repo.types.ts`, no base repo class; split at ~400 lines) exposes domain verbs and owns the query shape. Specs fake `<Entity>Repo` (`as unknown as <Entity>Repo`). Lock migrated modules with `no-restricted-imports` banning `PrismaService` in `**/*.service.ts`. When 2+ repos in a module share `select` shapes, extract `<module>/repos/<entity>.selects.ts` exporting `UPPER_SNAKE_SELECT as const` and re-exporting row types from `<module>.types.ts`. Cross-module/table-wide projection ownership follows `rules/prisma.md` #16–18: one select module per table in the owning domain, no cross-domain writes.

rules.title: Atomic side-effects & race-safe transitions
rules.content: 15. **Atomic side-effects & race-safe transitions** — Never leak a raw transaction to services: either the repo verb runs `$transaction` and invokes a `(tx, row) => Promise<unknown>` callback (`transitionWithBroadcast`), or the caller passes a scoped `PrismaTx` handle (`enqueueInTx(client, ...)`). Implement race-safe claims via `updateMany` with the expected status in `WHERE` and check `count === 0` (`STATE_CHANGED_CONCURRENTLY`).

rules.title: Prisma 7 `prisma-client` generator + `@prisma/client` alias
rules.content: 16. **Prisma 7 `prisma-client` generator + `@prisma/client` alias** — Generate into `src/generated/prisma` and map `@prisma/client` via tsconfig/Vitest regex alias (`rules/prisma.md`); never use legacy `prisma-client-js`.

rules.title: Unified `@nestjs/*` 12.x versioning & explicit `forRootAsync` arrays
rules.content: 17. **Unified `@nestjs/*` 12.x versioning & explicit `forRootAsync` arrays** — Upgrade all `@nestjs/*` core and satellite packages together (`@nestjs/http-client` versions independently). Always include `imports: []` and `providers: []` in `forRootAsync({...})` options to satisfy v12's stricter types (Precedent: XaDaoXa 2026-08, PR #226).

rules.title: `getOrThrow` for secrets & single Zod `env.schema.ts` on `ConfigModule`
rules.content:
18. **`getOrThrow` for secrets & single Zod `env.schema.ts` on `ConfigModule`** — Use `config.getOrThrow(key)` for required keys (never local `requireString` wrappers or `?? ''` mid-request fallbacks). Validate boot env via one Zod 4 Standard Schema passed to `ConfigModule.forRoot({ validationSchema: envSchema })` (never `validate` callback, which strips undeclared vars, and never Joi):
    - Schema owns types, requiredness, and defaults — config factories project/rename keys without re-declaring `||` fallbacks (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-10).
    - Preprocess empty `KEY=` strings (`'' → undefined`) so optional keys hit their schema default.
    - **Presence gates** (keys whose presence enables a vendor SDK/webhook) get **no default** (NestJS copies schema defaults into `process.env`); lock their absence in a spec. Put conditional rules (`FRONTEND_URL` https in prod) in `.superRefine`.

rules.title: Oxlint decorator config & `!: ` DI properties
rules.content: 19. **Oxlint decorator config & `!: ` DI properties** — Set `typescript/no-extraneous-class: ["warn", { "allowWithDecorator": true }]`. Property DI uses `private service!: Service` under `strict: true` (never disable `strictPropertyInitialization` or add `@ts-ignore`).

rules.title: Native CSRF header check (`app.enableCsrfProtection`), never `csurf`
rules.content: 20. **Native CSRF header check (`app.enableCsrfProtection`), never `csurf`** — Cookie-authenticated Nest apps call `app.enableCsrfProtection({ trustedOrigins })` (checks `Sec-Fetch-Site` / `Origin` vs `Host`; preserve `Host` behind proxies). Cookie-less APIs behind a Next 16 BFF enforce the `Origin` allowlist in BFF `src/proxy.ts` and keep zero CSRF middleware in the API. `csrf-csrf` requires an ADR (Precedent: VibeHost 2026-10, ADR-0018/0022).

rules.title: `@nestjs/http-client` only — never `axios`, `@nestjs/axios`, or raw `fetch`
`@nestjs/mail` for transactional email
rules.content: 22. **`@nestjs/mail` for transactional email** — Configure `MailModule.forRootAsync()` once in `AppModule`. Send `Mailable<TData>` classes via `Mailer.send(MailClass, { to, data, locale })` using built-in transports (`ResendTransport`, `SmtpTransport`, `SesTransport`, `FileMailTransport`, `InMemoryMailTransport`) and `FileTemplateEngine` (register template assets in `nest-cli.json#compilerOptions.assets`). Outbox consumers pass `idempotencyKey: message.id` and `retry: false`. In tests, assert via `mailbox.assertSent({ mail: MailClass })` — never regex raw HTML.

rules.title: `@nestjs/storage` for disks & uploads
rules.content: 23. **`@nestjs/storage` for disks & uploads** — Configure `StorageModule.forRootAsync()` once in `AppModule` (`LocalDisk`, `S3Disk`, `InMemoryDisk`) and inject `StorageDisk` / `@InjectDisk('name')`. Follow `rules/upload.md` for `uploadToDisk`, `serveFile`, `signedUrl`, and media lifecycle.

rules.title: Bounded in-memory `Map`s & disconnect-aware SSE streams
rules.content: 24. **Bounded in-memory `Map`s & disconnect-aware SSE streams** — Every stateful `Map` (login failures, rate buckets, caches) must enforce `MAX_ENTRIES`, TTL pruning, and FIFO eviction (`if (this.cache.size >= MAX_ENTRIES) this.cache.delete(this.cache.keys().next().value)`). SSE/streaming endpoints must attach `res.once('close', () => abortController.abort())`, pass `AbortSignal` to registry waiters, and implement `OnModuleDestroy` (Precedent: XaDaoXa 2026-09).

rules.title: Issuance choke-point guards, delegated profile resolution, self-sorting helpers & Vitest timer restore
rules.content:
25. **Issuance choke-point guards, delegated profile resolution, self-sorting helpers & Vitest timer restore** —
    - Enforce principal status checks (blacklist, suspension, lockout) inside the shared token/session issuer (`AuthIssuerService.issueTokens`, `SessionService.rotate` *before* `session.create`), never per-strategy (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-10).
    - In multi-profile or family-linked systems where a session switches profiles via `activeProfileId`, resolve the target principal on profile-scoped endpoints (`/users/profile`, `/notifications`, `/sessions/schedule`, `/lms/*`) via `user.activeProfileId ?? user.id` rather than raw `user.id` (keep raw `user.id` only on account-level security/billing actions — Precedent: Gia Su Anh Minh 2026-10).
    - Pure progression/threshold helpers (`resolveTierProgression`) sort their own input or call a direction-named repo verb (`listTiersDesc`) rather than trusting implicit repo sort order.
    - When `vitest.config.ts` sets `isolate: false`, register `afterAll(() => { vi.useRealTimers() })` in `setupFiles` (never global `afterEach`, which breaks multi-`describe` specs sharing a `beforeEach` clock) AND pair every per-file `vi.useFakeTimers()` with `afterEach`/`afterAll` restore so leaked `@sinonjs/fake-timers` never hang stream or multi-file multer `setImmediate` cleanup in subsequent specs (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-10, PR #452).

10. **Split request DTOs from response/shared types** — Request contracts live in `module_name/dto/*.dto.ts`; response shapes, pagination wrappers, and cross-module row types live in `module_name/<module>.types.ts`.
<!-- rule: relative-when-shorter-import -->
11. **Relative-when-shorter imports** — Import across folders via `@/<folder>/...` unless the relative path (`../dto/create-video.dto`) is shorter; import defining files directly and keep same-folder imports relative.
<!-- rule: import-global-infra-modules -->
12. **Import `@Global()` infra modules once in `AppModule`** — Never re-import `PrismaInfraModule`, `ClsModule`, or `ConfigModule` in child modules.
<!-- rule: break-x-y-x-module-cycles-wi -->
13. **Break `X → Y → X` module cycles with a neutral `*CoreModule`** — Extract dependency-free providers into `*CoreModule` imported by both sides; never re-register foreign `{ provide: TOKEN, useClass }` bindings or reach for `forwardRef()` (Precedent: TaxEasy 2026-08).

## Repository seam & Prisma 7 (mandatory)

<!-- rule: flat-domain-verb-repos-modul -->
14. **Flat domain-verb repos (`module_name/repo/<name>.repo.ts`), class is the contract** — Services never inject `PrismaService` directly. Each repo class (`<Entity>Repo` — no `Prisma` prefix, no `Repository` suffix, no `I*Repository` interface, no `repo/index.ts` barrel, no `*.repo.types.ts`, no base repo class; split at ~400 lines) exposes domain verbs and owns the query shape. Specs fake `<Entity>Repo` (`as unknown as <Entity>Repo`). Lock migrated modules with `no-restricted-imports` banning `PrismaService` in `**/*.service.ts`. When 2+ repos in a module share `select` shapes, extract `<module>/repos/<entity>.selects.ts` exporting `UPPER_SNAKE_SELECT as const` and re-exporting row types from `<module>.types.ts`. Cross-module/table-wide projection ownership follows `rules/prisma.md` #16–18: one select module per table in the owning domain, no cross-domain writes.
<!-- rule: atomic-side-effects-and-race -->
15. **Atomic side-effects & race-safe transitions** — Never leak a raw transaction to services: either the repo verb runs `$transaction` and invokes a `(tx, row) => Promise<unknown>` callback (`transitionWithBroadcast`), or the caller passes a scoped `PrismaTx` handle (`enqueueInTx(client, ...)`). Implement race-safe claims via `updateMany` with the expected status in `WHERE` and check `count === 0` (`STATE_CHANGED_CONCURRENTLY`).
<!-- rule: prisma-7-prisma-client-gener -->
16. **Prisma 7 `prisma-client` generator + `@prisma/client` alias** — Generate into `src/generated/prisma` and map `@prisma/client` via tsconfig/Vitest regex alias (`rules/prisma.md`); never use legacy `prisma-client-js`.

## NestJS 12, env config & linting (mandatory)

<!-- rule: unified-nestjs-12x-versionin -->
17. **Unified `@nestjs/*` 12.x versioning & explicit `forRootAsync` arrays** — Upgrade all `@nestjs/*` core and satellite packages together (`@nestjs/http-client` versions independently). Always include `imports: []` and `providers: []` in `forRootAsync({...})` options to satisfy v12's stricter types (Precedent: XaDaoXa 2026-08, PR #226).
<!-- rule: getorthrow-for-secrets-and-s -->
18. **`getOrThrow` for secrets & single Zod `env.schema.ts` on `ConfigModule`** — Use `config.getOrThrow(key)` for required keys (never local `requireString` wrappers or `?? ''` mid-request fallbacks). Validate boot env via one Zod 4 Standard Schema passed to `ConfigModule.forRoot({ validationSchema: envSchema })` (never `validate` callback, which strips undeclared vars, and never Joi):
    - Schema owns types, requiredness, and defaults — config factories project/rename keys without re-declaring `||` fallbacks (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-10).
    - Preprocess empty `KEY=` strings (`'' → undefined`) so optional keys hit their schema default.
    - **Presence gates** (keys whose presence enables a vendor SDK/webhook) get **no default** (NestJS copies schema defaults into `process.env`); lock their absence in a spec. Put conditional rules (`FRONTEND_URL` https in prod) in `.superRefine`.
<!-- rule: oxlint-decorator-config-and -->
19. **Oxlint decorator config & `!: ` DI properties** — Set `typescript/no-extraneous-class: ["warn", { "allowWithDecorator": true }]`. Property DI uses `private service!: Service` under `strict: true` (never disable `strictPropertyInitialization` or add `@ts-ignore`).

## CSRF, HTTP client, Mail & Storage (mandatory)

<!-- rule: native-csrf-header-check-app -->
20. **Native CSRF header check (`app.enableCsrfProtection`), never `csurf`** — Cookie-authenticated Nest apps call `app.enableCsrfProtection({ trustedOrigins })` (checks `Sec-Fetch-Site` / `Origin` vs `Host`; preserve `Host` behind proxies). Cookie-less APIs behind a Next 16 BFF enforce the `Origin` allowlist in BFF `src/proxy.ts` and keep zero CSRF middleware in the API. `csrf-csrf` requires an ADR (Precedent: VibeHost 2026-10, ADR-0018/0022).
<!-- rule: nestjshttp-client-only-never -->
21. **`@nestjs/http-client` only — never `axios`, `@nestjs/axios`, or raw `fetch`** — Configure `HttpClientModule.forRoot({ retry: false, timeout: 10_000 })` once and `.register({ name, baseUrl, retry: false })` per upstream; inject via `@InjectHttpClient(name)`:

    ```ts
    const { data } = await this.http.post<Created>('/users', { json: { email } });
    // Errors: branch via instanceof HttpResponseError / HttpNetworkError / HttpTimeoutError
    // Tests: pass `fetch: stubFetch` in register() or .overrideProvider(getHttpClientToken('name'))
    ```

    Pass `json` or raw `body` (never both), `query` for search params, `params` for `:segment` (Precedent: VibeHost 2026-10).
<!-- rule: nestjsmail-for-transactional -->
22. **`@nestjs/mail` for transactional email** — Configure `MailModule.forRootAsync()` once in `AppModule`. Send `Mailable<TData>` classes via `Mailer.send(MailClass, { to, data, locale })` using built-in transports (`ResendTransport`, `SmtpTransport`, `SesTransport`, `FileMailTransport`, `InMemoryMailTransport`) and `FileTemplateEngine` (register template assets in `nest-cli.json#compilerOptions.assets`). Outbox consumers pass `idempotencyKey: message.id` and `retry: false`. In tests, assert via `mailbox.assertSent({ mail: MailClass })` — never regex raw HTML.
<!-- rule: nestjsstorage-for-disks-and -->
23. **`@nestjs/storage` for disks & uploads** — Configure `StorageModule.forRootAsync()` once in `AppModule` (`LocalDisk`, `S3Disk`, `InMemoryDisk`) and inject `StorageDisk` / `@InjectDisk('name')`. Follow `rules/upload.md` for `uploadToDisk`, `serveFile`, `signedUrl`, and media lifecycle.

## Runtime bounds, choke-point invariants & Vitest isolation (mandatory)

<!-- rule: bounded-in-memory-maps-and-d -->
24. **Bounded in-memory `Map`s & disconnect-aware SSE streams** — Every stateful `Map` (login failures, rate buckets, caches) must enforce `MAX_ENTRIES`, TTL pruning, and FIFO eviction (`if (this.cache.size >= MAX_ENTRIES) this.cache.delete(this.cache.keys().next().value)`). SSE/streaming endpoints must attach `res.once('close', () => abortController.abort())`, pass `AbortSignal` to registry waiters, and implement `OnModuleDestroy` (Precedent: XaDaoXa 2026-09).
<!-- rule: issuance-choke-point-guards -->
25. **Issuance choke-point guards, delegated profile resolution, self-sorting helpers & Vitest timer restore** —
    - Enforce principal status checks (blacklist, suspension, lockout) inside the shared token/session issuer (`AuthIssuerService.issueTokens`, `SessionService.rotate` *before* `session.create`), never per-strategy (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-10).
    - In multi-profile or family-linked systems where a session switches profiles via `activeProfileId`, resolve the target principal on profile-scoped endpoints (`/users/profile`, `/notifications`, `/sessions/schedule`, `/lms/*`) via `user.activeProfileId ?? user.id` rather than raw `user.id` (keep raw `user.id` only on account-level security/billing actions — Precedent: Gia Su Anh Minh 2026-10).
    - Pure progression/threshold helpers (`resolveTierProgression`) sort their own input or call a direction-named repo verb (`listTiersDesc`) rather than trusting implicit repo sort order.
    - When `vitest.config.ts` sets `isolate: false`, register `afterAll(() => { vi.useRealTimers() })` in `setupFiles` (never global `afterEach`, which breaks multi-`describe` specs sharing a `beforeEach` clock) AND pair every per-file `vi.useFakeTimers()` with `afterEach`/`afterAll` restore so leaked `@sinonjs/fake-timers` never hang stream or multi-file multer `setImmediate` cleanup in subsequent specs (Precedent: Ecopick 2026-10, PR #452).

entries.title: Prisma 7 — client setup & writing rules
entries.name: Prisma 7 — client setup & writing rules
entries.description: Applies to every TypeScript/NestJS project on Prisma ORM 7. Overrides the legacy `prisma-client-js` principle (v6-era: client generated into `node_modules/@prisma/client`, no adapter). MongoDB projects stay on Prisma 6.x — do not apply this module to them.
entries.scope: TS/NestJS repos on Prisma 7

rules.title: Module context
rules.content:
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to every TypeScript/NestJS project on Prisma ORM 7. Overrides the legacy `prisma-client-js` principle (v6-era: client generated into `node_modules/@prisma/client`, no adapter). MongoDB projects stay on Prisma 6.x — do not apply this module to them.

rules.title: `prisma-client` generator + source-tree output, never `prisma-client-js` for new work
`prisma.config.ts` owns env + database URL
Regenerate with `pnpm prisma generate`
rules.content: 3. **Regenerate with `pnpm prisma generate`** — output goes to `src/generated/prisma` and must stay gitignored (`.gitignore`: `generated/` matches at any depth). At build time `nest build` (swc) compiles the generated TS and rewrites the alias to relative requires, so runtime `node dist/main.js` needs no tsconfig-paths shim.

rules.title: Import from the `@prisma/client` specifier via path alias
Vitest aliases MUST use the regex form
Files outside `src/` keep the same specifier
rules.content: 6. **Files outside `src/` keep the same specifier** — seed and `scripts/*.ts` resolve via tsconfig paths under `tsx`, but are outside the compiled program; only `src/` files are guaranteed rewrites.

rules.title: Driver adapter is mandatory
rules.content: 7. **Driver adapter is mandatory** — `new PrismaClient({ adapter: new PrismaPg({ connectionString }) })`; pool sizing lives on the adapter (`max`, `idleTimeoutMillis`, `connectionTimeoutMillis`), never in `datasource.url` query strings. One adapter per client instance — primary + bare/system client = two adapters, no shared pool.

rules.title: Type-safe query fragments use `satisfies`, never `Prisma.validator`
rules.content: 8. **Type-safe query fragments use `satisfies`, never `Prisma.validator`** — `Prisma.validator` is removed; `{ id: true } satisfies Prisma.UserSelect` is the replacement.

rules.title: Middleware is gone
rules.content: 9. **Middleware is gone** — `$use()` is removed; custom behavior rides Client Extensions (`$extends`) or query extension on the client type. Do not reintroduce middleware-style hooks.

rules.title: Tenant scoping on the client type
rules.content: 10. **Tenant scoping on the client type** — extensions (`$extends`) compose on `PrismaClient` via the generated `client` entrypoint; `PrismaService extends PrismaClient` with a `bareClient` for system ops (cron, raw SQL) is the canonical shape; `$queryRaw`/`$executeRaw` stay on the bare instance.

rules.title: Transactions
rules.content: 11. **Transactions** — `$transaction` interactive callbacks are the standard; race-safe transitions use `updateMany` with expected-state predicates (see `rules/nestjs.md` rule 15).

rules.title: No runtime statutory config in DB
rules.content: 12. **No runtime statutory config in DB** — tax rates/feature thresholds resolve from the hardcoded versioned ledger, not from `prisma` reads (ADR 0042 pattern).

rules.title: Every model change ships a migration in the same commit
rules.content: 13. **Every model change ships a migration in the same commit** — `prisma validate` and `prisma format` do not compare `prisma/models/**` with `prisma/migrations`. CI's `migrate reset` applies migrations only, so a model edit without a migration passes validation and fails at runtime on the first query that reads the new column (`P2022`). `db push` development hides this. Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — 13 columns, the e2e seed failed on `marketing_opt_in`.

rules.title: CI fails on schema/migration drift
rules.content:
14. **CI fails on schema/migration drift** — Add to the `prisma` job:
    ```sh
    bun x prisma migrate diff --from-migrations prisma/migrations --to-schema prisma --exit-code
    ```
    Exit `0` is in sync, `2` is drift. `migrate status` compares applied migration rows, not the schema, so it does not catch this.

rules.title: A blank or wrong-looking field on the client is often a `select` that never joined the relation — check the server response before patching the client fallback.
rules.content: 15. **A blank or wrong-looking field on the client is often a `select` that never joined the relation — check the server response before patching the client fallback.** A frontend `sellerName: raw.sellerName ?? ''` mapper is a symptom, not a bug, if `raw.sellerName` was never sent because the endpoint's `select` (a shared `MANAGE_SELECT`/`LIST_SELECT` object, or an inline one) never included `seller: { select: { citizen: { select: { fullName: true } } } }` in the first place. Compare against a peer endpoint that renders the same underlying data correctly (a detail vs. list variant of the same entity, an admin vs. public read) before assuming the bug is in the mapper — a `select` shape shared across list/detail/create/update endpoints (`rules/nestjs.md` rule 14) missing one relation produces the identical gap on every consumer of that shape, not just the one screen where it was first noticed.

rules.title: One select module per table with named variants
rules.content: 16. **One select module per table with named variants** — Each table has one canonical projection module in its owning domain (`<table>.select.ts`) with named variants (`Public`, `Self`, `Admin`, `Search`) and `satisfies Prisma.<Model>Select`. Other modules import or extend that module; they never redefine the table's shape. One table must not have several private select copies that drift.

rules.title: No cross-domain Prisma writes; reads go through the owner
rules.content: 17. **No cross-domain Prisma writes; reads go through the owner** — A domain writes only its own tables. A cross-domain write goes through the owning domain's write port; a cross-domain read goes through an owner read function or port. Admin dashboards and reports are not an exception. Enforce with dependency-cruiser or a lint map when the repo has one; otherwise grep `prisma.<table>` outside the owner path in review.

rules.title: Consolidating a select is a behavior change until proven otherwise
rules.content: 18. **Consolidating a select is a behavior change until proven otherwise** — Replacing a local select with a shared variant must preserve the exact field set. An additive field is still a response change; state it in the PR and test the affected endpoint. Do not delete a field to make the shared shape fit.

id: "prisma"
name: "Prisma 7 — client setup & writing rules"
kind: "rule"
description: "Applies to every TypeScript/NestJS project on Prisma ORM 7. Overrides the legacy `prisma-client-js` principle (v6-era: client generated into `node_modules/@prisma/client`, no adapter). MongoDB projects stay on Prisma 6.x — do not apply this module to them."
scope: "TS/NestJS repos on Prisma 7"
priority: "mandatory"
---
# Prisma 7 — client setup & writing rules

<!-- rule: module-context -->
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to every TypeScript/NestJS project on Prisma ORM 7. Overrides the legacy `prisma-client-js` principle (v6-era: client generated into `node_modules/@prisma/client`, no adapter). MongoDB projects stay on Prisma 6.x — do not apply this module to them.

## Generator output (mandatory)

<!-- rule: prisma-client-generator-sour -->
1. **`prisma-client` generator + source-tree output, never `prisma-client-js` for new work** — `prisma-client-js` (generates into `node_modules/@prisma/client`) is a migration-only fallback. Canonical base `schema.prisma` (TaxEasy `apps/api` 2026-08):

```prisma
// prisma/schema.prisma — v7 base (no url/directUrl in datasource; they live in prisma.config.ts)
generator client {
  provider        = "prisma-client"
  output          = "../src/generated/prisma"
  moduleFormat    = "cjs"          // CJS apps; omit for ESM
  previewFeatures = ["partialIndexes"]
}

datasource db {
  provider   = "postgresql"
  extensions = [unaccent, vector] // postgresqlExtensions preview feature
}
```

<!-- rule: prismaconfigts-owns-env-data -->
2. **`prisma.config.ts` owns env + database URL** — the schema `datasource` block keeps only `provider` + extensions; `url`/`directUrl`/`shadowDatabaseUrl` move here:

```typescript
import "dotenv/config";
import { defineConfig } from "prisma/config";

export default defineConfig({
  schema: "prisma",
  datasource: {
    url: process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? "",
  },
  migrations: {
    path: "prisma/migrations",
    seed: "pnpm tsx prisma/seed/index.ts",
  },
});
```

<!-- rule: regenerate-with-pnpm-prisma -->
3. **Regenerate with `pnpm prisma generate`** — output goes to `src/generated/prisma` and must stay gitignored (`.gitignore`: `generated/` matches at any depth). At build time `nest build` (swc) compiles the generated TS and rewrites the alias to relative requires, so runtime `node dist/main.js` needs no tsconfig-paths shim.

## `@prisma/client` alias (mandatory)

<!-- rule: import-from-the-prismaclient -->
4. **Import from the `@prisma/client` specifier via path alias** — nothing is generated into node_modules, so the specifier must be mapped in every resolver (tsc/swc keys are EXACT, so the generated client's internal `@prisma/client/runtime/client` falls through to node_modules untouched):

```jsonc
// tsconfig.json
"paths": {
  "@/*": ["./src/*"],
  "@prisma/client": ["./src/generated/prisma/client.ts"]
}
```

<!-- rule: vitest-aliases-must-use-the -->
5. **Vitest aliases MUST use the regex form** — in `vitest.config.ts` AND `vitest.integration.config.ts`. Vite object-form keys are **prefix-matched**: a string key `'@prisma/client'` also swallows `@prisma/client/runtime/client` (imported by the generated client itself), rewriting it into `client.ts/runtime/client` and breaking every spec (159/159 failed until fixed):

```typescript
resolve: {
  alias: [
    { find: '@', replacement: path.resolve(__dirname, 'src') },
    { find: /^@prisma\/client$/, replacement: path.resolve(__dirname, 'src/generated/prisma/client.ts') },
  ],
},
```

<!-- rule: files-outside-src-keep-the-s -->
6. **Files outside `src/` keep the same specifier** — seed and `scripts/*.ts` resolve via tsconfig paths under `tsx`, but are outside the compiled program; only `src/` files are guaranteed rewrites.

## Writing Prisma code on v7 (mandatory)

<!-- rule: driver-adapter-is-mandatory -->
7. **Driver adapter is mandatory** — `new PrismaClient({ adapter: new PrismaPg({ connectionString }) })`; pool sizing lives on the adapter (`max`, `idleTimeoutMillis`, `connectionTimeoutMillis`), never in `datasource.url` query strings. One adapter per client instance — primary + bare/system client = two adapters, no shared pool.

<!-- rule: type-safe-query-fragments-us -->
8. **Type-safe query fragments use `satisfies`, never `Prisma.validator`** — `Prisma.validator` is removed; `{ id: true } satisfies Prisma.UserSelect` is the replacement.

<!-- rule: middleware-is-gone -->
9. **Middleware is gone** — `$use()` is removed; custom behavior rides Client Extensions (`$extends`) or query extension on the client type. Do not reintroduce middleware-style hooks.

<!-- rule: tenant-scoping-on-the-client -->
10. **Tenant scoping on the client type** — extensions (`$extends`) compose on `PrismaClient` via the generated `client` entrypoint; `PrismaService extends PrismaClient` with a `bareClient` for system ops (cron, raw SQL) is the canonical shape; `$queryRaw`/`$executeRaw` stay on the bare instance.

<!-- rule: transactions -->
11. **Transactions** — `$transaction` interactive callbacks are the standard; race-safe transitions use `updateMany` with expected-state predicates (see `rules/nestjs.md` rule 15).

<!-- rule: no-runtime-statutory-config -->
12. **No runtime statutory config in DB** — tax rates/feature thresholds resolve from the hardcoded versioned ledger, not from `prisma` reads (ADR 0042 pattern).

## Migrations (mandatory)

<!-- rule: every-model-change-ships-a-m -->
13. **Every model change ships a migration in the same commit** — `prisma validate` and `prisma format` do not compare `prisma/models/**` with `prisma/migrations`. CI's `migrate reset` applies migrations only, so a model edit without a migration passes validation and fails at runtime on the first query that reads the new column (`P2022`). `db push` development hides this. Precedent: Ecopick 2026-11 — 13 columns, the e2e seed failed on `marketing_opt_in`.

<!-- rule: ci-fails-on-schemamigration -->
14. **CI fails on schema/migration drift** — Add to the `prisma` job:
    ```sh
    bun x prisma migrate diff --from-migrations prisma/migrations --to-schema prisma --exit-code
    ```
    Exit `0` is in sync, `2` is drift. `migrate status` compares applied migration rows, not the schema, so it does not catch this.

## Diagnosing a blank/wrong client field (mandatory)

<!-- rule: a-blank-or-wrong-looking-fie -->
15. **A blank or wrong-looking field on the client is often a `select` that never joined the relation — check the server response before patching the client fallback.** A frontend `sellerName: raw.sellerName ?? ''` mapper is a symptom, not a bug, if `raw.sellerName` was never sent because the endpoint's `select` (a shared `MANAGE_SELECT`/`LIST_SELECT` object, or an inline one) never included `seller: { select: { citizen: { select: { fullName: true } } } }` in the first place. Compare against a peer endpoint that renders the same underlying data correctly (a detail vs. list variant of the same entity, an admin vs. public read) before assuming the bug is in the mapper — a `select` shape shared across list/detail/create/update endpoints (`rules/nestjs.md` rule 14) missing one relation produces the identical gap on every consumer of that shape, not just the one screen where it was first noticed.

## Projection ownership (mandatory)

<!-- rule: one-select-module-per-table -->
16. **One select module per table with named variants** — Each table has one canonical projection module in its owning domain (`<table>.select.ts`) with named variants (`Public`, `Self`, `Admin`, `Search`) and `satisfies Prisma.<Model>Select`. Other modules import or extend that module; they never redefine the table's shape. One table must not have several private select copies that drift.
<!-- rule: no-cross-domain-prisma-write -->
17. **No cross-domain Prisma writes; reads go through the owner** — A domain writes only its own tables. A cross-domain write goes through the owning domain's write port; a cross-domain read goes through an owner read function or port. Admin dashboards and reports are not an exception. Enforce with dependency-cruiser or a lint map when the repo has one; otherwise grep `prisma.<table>` outside the owner path in review.
<!-- rule: consolidating-a-select-is-a -->
18. **Consolidating a select is a behavior change until proven otherwise** — Replacing a local select with a shared variant must preserve the exact field set. An additive field is still a response change; state it in the PR and test the affected endpoint. Do not delete a field to make the shared shape fit.

entries.title: QA & UI Consistency Rules
entries.name: QA & UI Consistency Rules
entries.description: For projects with Next.js-style frontends (server + client component split), a seeded dev database, and a
entries.scope: Next.js-style frontends with a screenshot QA harness over seeded data

rules.title: Module context
rules.content:
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

For projects with Next.js-style frontends (server + client component split), a seeded dev database, and a
screenshot-based QA harness (full-page sweeps at multiple device widths reviewed by agents or humans).
Rules proven by a full-app QA pass that found ~35 defects; each rule cites its incident.

rules.title: Serializable props only.
rules.content:
1. **Serializable props only.** A server component must never pass a function prop to a client component —
   it renders fine in isolation but throws "Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components" when
   the page composes (found live: a log list took `levelLabel: (lv) => string` and its server page passed a
   closure over `getTranslations()`; the whole page 500'd). Type client props as plain data —
   `Record<Level, string>` built by the caller from translations — so both server and client callers compile
   against the same shape. The type system accepts the function; the review check is "does any server page
   hand a closure across a client boundary?".

rules.title: Page status codes hide runtime 500s.
rules.content:
2. **Page status codes hide runtime 500s.** An error boundary answers 200, so a sweep manifest can pass a
   broken page. QA tooling must also flag error-boundary copy in the body, and dev-server logs must be
   tee'd to a file — the log is where the 500 actually surfaced.

rules.title: Interpolation slots take the value their grammar says.
rules.content:
3. **Interpolation slots take the value their grammar says.** A destination slot got a full sentence and
   rendered "Tới Sau khi đăng nhập, bạn quay lại" on three screens (the label meant "after sign-in you
   return to …"). When a message is only ever rendered one way, hardcode the context into the message and
   keep the count/time slots only.

rules.title: One source of truth for numbers in copy.
rules.content:
4. **One source of truth for numbers in copy.** A hardcoded "100.000đ" inside a message drifted from the
   code's `WITHDRAW_MIN = 200_000` and contradicted the page's own rules text. Parameterize
   (`"đạt {min} — còn thiếu {amount}"`) and pass the constant.

rules.title: Every locale catalog gets every key.
rules.content:
5. **Every locale catalog gets every key.** New user-facing copy lands in all locale files in the same
   commit; the i18n key checker fails the build otherwise. A 404 page shipped hardcoded English on a
   Vietnamese-default product for its whole life because nobody ran the check on static pages.

rules.title: One predicate per visual state.
rules.content:
6. **One predicate per visual state.** Every indicator answering the same question must derive from one
   predicate: the inbox shipped "2 unread" against four unread dots because dots counted status tiles
   (`type === "attention" || readAt === null`) while the counter, filter, and mark-all counted notification
   rows only. Status tiles are not unread mail.

rules.title: Empty values render as designed states.
rules.content:
7. **Empty values render as designed states.** Missing data renders as a placeholder — avatar initials, an
   image-icon tile, "—", "Chưa có" — never as: `<Image src="">` (a console error per row), a "— › —"
   breadcrumb, a dangling "• Label" with no value, a "·" line with both sides empty, or a date formatted
   without an explicit locale (US "11/15/2026" on a vi product). Null expires-at maps to "—", not to a
   negative number or a crash.

rules.title: Disabled keeps its silhouette.
rules.content:
8. **Disabled keeps its silhouette.** A disabled CTA keeps its enabled styling (solid primary / outlined
   secondary) at reduced opacity with `cursor-not-allowed`. `border-transparent opacity-50` reads as broken
   text; staff could not tell a disabled button from missing markup.

rules.title: Raw validation/dev strings never reach the UI.
rules.content:
9. **Raw validation/dev strings never reach the UI.** An env-var row rendered its rule as
   "nullable|string|max:64" — the developer's schema leaked into staff-facing copy. Human text only
   ("Tuỳ chọn · tối đa 64 ký tự").

rules.title: Live-or-fixture, never half-blank.
rules.content:
10. **Live-or-fixture, never half-blank.** Server pages read live data through a cookie+contract fetch that
    returns null on any failure, falling back to the seeded fixture — a logged-out preview never blanks.
    Mind identity spaces when wiring a fixture page live: live row ids are usernames, fixture ids may differ
    (`linh.d` vs `qa-rs-01`) — match on the live id. If no endpoint exists, keep the fixture and name the
    missing endpoint in the docstring.

rules.title: Seed identity links are load-bearing.
rules.content:
11. **Seed identity links are load-bearing.** Admin-style guards that match an env-pinned ID list against a
    linked identity (Discord `providerId`) break silently when the seed reshapes: every privileged endpoint
    403s while pages still render shells, and screenshots look almost normal. The seed must recreate the
    identity links on every run, and the QA harness must smoke-test one privileged endpoint before sweeping.

rules.title: Migrations must replay from zero and match the schema.
rules.content:
12. **Migrations must replay from zero and match the schema.** A committed migration ALTERed two tables no
    migration creates, and two schema models shipped without any migration — both landed with CI green
    (lint/typecheck/test/build do not catch it). A shadow-database replay diff is the standing check.

rules.title: Ground truth is the DOM.
rules.content:
13. **Ground truth is the DOM.** Full-page screenshots are downscaled during review; fused text, phantom
    truncations, and wrong-glyph reads are common (three audit findings retracted after DOM checks). A claim
    made from pixels is low-confidence until verified in the DOM or source.

rules.title: Triage the manifest before reading screenshots.
rules.content:
14. **Triage the manifest before reading screenshots.** Statuses, per-shot console errors, and final URLs
    carry the infra failures (broken seed → 403s everywhere, stale route lists → redirects, empty-src
    images → per-row warnings). Auditing a half-broken stack wastes the entire pass.

rules.title: Archive the previous sweep.
rules.content:
15. **Archive the previous sweep.** Before/after trees are how a fix is proven; overwriting loses the
    comparison and the re-shoot becomes assertion instead of evidence.

rules.title: Exception states are mocked, not trusted; runtime values use logpoints.
rules.content:
16. **Exception states are mocked, not trusted; runtime values use logpoints.** A seeded sweep only ever
    exercises happy paths — code review never proves the error UI. Force the failure in the live browser
    through Chrome DevTools MCP: `mock_network` serves a local fixture `body` in place of a real API
    response, or redirects a route's `upstream` to a stub server returning the real status and headers
    (a 5xx body, or a dead endpoint to simulate a failed request); re-shoot the page and audit the error
    state against rule 7. Configure mocks before navigating, check hit counts with a filter-less
    `mock_network` call, remove them with `remove_network_mock` after (mocks disable the HTTP cache and
    skew any perf measurement), and mind that service workers can bypass mocks. When diagnosing what a
    line actually saw, set `set_logpoints` on the source location (resolved via source maps; output lands
    in `list_console_messages`) instead of editing in a `console.log` and waiting for a rebuild.

# QA & UI Consistency Rules

<!-- rule: module-context -->
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

For projects with Next.js-style frontends (server + client component split), a seeded dev database, and a
screenshot-based QA harness (full-page sweeps at multiple device widths reviewed by agents or humans).
Rules proven by a full-app QA pass that found ~35 defects; each rule cites its incident.

## Server → client component boundaries

<!-- rule: serializable-props-only -->
1. **Serializable props only.** A server component must never pass a function prop to a client component —
   it renders fine in isolation but throws "Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components" when
   the page composes (found live: a log list took `levelLabel: (lv) => string` and its server page passed a
   closure over `getTranslations()`; the whole page 500'd). Type client props as plain data —
   `Record<Level, string>` built by the caller from translations — so both server and client callers compile
   against the same shape. The type system accepts the function; the review check is "does any server page
   hand a closure across a client boundary?".

<!-- rule: page-status-codes-hide-runti -->
2. **Page status codes hide runtime 500s.** An error boundary answers 200, so a sweep manifest can pass a
   broken page. QA tooling must also flag error-boundary copy in the body, and dev-server logs must be
   tee'd to a file — the log is where the 500 actually surfaced.

## Copy and i18n

<!-- rule: interpolation-slots-take-the -->
3. **Interpolation slots take the value their grammar says.** A destination slot got a full sentence and
   rendered "Tới Sau khi đăng nhập, bạn quay lại" on three screens (the label meant "after sign-in you
   return to …"). When a message is only ever rendered one way, hardcode the context into the message and
   keep the count/time slots only.

<!-- rule: one-source-of-truth-for-numb -->
4. **One source of truth for numbers in copy.** A hardcoded "100.000đ" inside a message drifted from the
   code's `WITHDRAW_MIN = 200_000` and contradicted the page's own rules text. Parameterize
   (`"đạt {min} — còn thiếu {amount}"`) and pass the constant.

<!-- rule: every-locale-catalog-gets-ev -->
5. **Every locale catalog gets every key.** New user-facing copy lands in all locale files in the same
   commit; the i18n key checker fails the build otherwise. A 404 page shipped hardcoded English on a
   Vietnamese-default product for its whole life because nobody ran the check on static pages.

## State rendering

<!-- rule: one-predicate-per-visual-sta -->
6. **One predicate per visual state.** Every indicator answering the same question must derive from one
   predicate: the inbox shipped "2 unread" against four unread dots because dots counted status tiles
   (`type === "attention" || readAt === null`) while the counter, filter, and mark-all counted notification
   rows only. Status tiles are not unread mail.

<!-- rule: empty-values-render-as-desig -->
7. **Empty values render as designed states.** Missing data renders as a placeholder — avatar initials, an
   image-icon tile, "—", "Chưa có" — never as: `<Image src="">` (a console error per row), a "— › —"
   breadcrumb, a dangling "• Label" with no value, a "·" line with both sides empty, or a date formatted
   without an explicit locale (US "11/15/2026" on a vi product). Null expires-at maps to "—", not to a
   negative number or a crash.

<!-- rule: disabled-keeps-its-silhouett -->
8. **Disabled keeps its silhouette.** A disabled CTA keeps its enabled styling (solid primary / outlined
   secondary) at reduced opacity with `cursor-not-allowed`. `border-transparent opacity-50` reads as broken
   text; staff could not tell a disabled button from missing markup.

<!-- rule: raw-validationdev-strings-ne -->
9. **Raw validation/dev strings never reach the UI.** An env-var row rendered its rule as
   "nullable|string|max:64" — the developer's schema leaked into staff-facing copy. Human text only
   ("Tuỳ chọn · tối đa 64 ký tự").

## Fixture and seed discipline

<!-- rule: live-or-fixture-never-half-b -->
10. **Live-or-fixture, never half-blank.** Server pages read live data through a cookie+contract fetch that
    returns null on any failure, falling back to the seeded fixture — a logged-out preview never blanks.
    Mind identity spaces when wiring a fixture page live: live row ids are usernames, fixture ids may differ
    (`linh.d` vs `qa-rs-01`) — match on the live id. If no endpoint exists, keep the fixture and name the
    missing endpoint in the docstring.

<!-- rule: seed-identity-links-are-load -->
11. **Seed identity links are load-bearing.** Admin-style guards that match an env-pinned ID list against a
    linked identity (Discord `providerId`) break silently when the seed reshapes: every privileged endpoint
    403s while pages still render shells, and screenshots look almost normal. The seed must recreate the
    identity links on every run, and the QA harness must smoke-test one privileged endpoint before sweeping.

<!-- rule: migrations-must-replay-from -->
12. **Migrations must replay from zero and match the schema.** A committed migration ALTERed two tables no
    migration creates, and two schema models shipped without any migration — both landed with CI green
    (lint/typecheck/test/build do not catch it). A shadow-database replay diff is the standing check.

## QA harness discipline

<!-- rule: ground-truth-is-the-dom -->
13. **Ground truth is the DOM.** Full-page screenshots are downscaled during review; fused text, phantom
    truncations, and wrong-glyph reads are common (three audit findings retracted after DOM checks). A claim
    made from pixels is low-confidence until verified in the DOM or source.

<!-- rule: triage-the-manifest-before-r -->
14. **Triage the manifest before reading screenshots.** Statuses, per-shot console errors, and final URLs
    carry the infra failures (broken seed → 403s everywhere, stale route lists → redirects, empty-src
    images → per-row warnings). Auditing a half-broken stack wastes the entire pass.

<!-- rule: archive-the-previous-sweep -->
15. **Archive the previous sweep.** Before/after trees are how a fix is proven; overwriting loses the
    comparison and the re-shoot becomes assertion instead of evidence.

<!-- rule: exception-states-are-mocked -->
16. **Exception states are mocked, not trusted; runtime values use logpoints.** A seeded sweep only ever
    exercises happy paths — code review never proves the error UI. Force the failure in the live browser
    through Chrome DevTools MCP: `mock_network` serves a local fixture `body` in place of a real API
    response, or redirects a route's `upstream` to a stub server returning the real status and headers
    (a 5xx body, or a dead endpoint to simulate a failed request); re-shoot the page and audit the error
    state against rule 7. Configure mocks before navigating, check hit counts with a filter-less
    `mock_network` call, remove them with `remove_network_mock` after (mocks disable the HTTP cache and
    skew any perf measurement), and mind that service workers can bypass mocks. When diagnosing what a
    line actually saw, set `set_logpoints` on the source location (resolved via source maps; output lands
    in `list_console_messages`) instead of editing in a `console.log` and waiting for a rebuild.

entries.title: Real-User QA Rules — Functional browser pass
entries.name: Real-User QA Rules — Functional browser pass
entries.description: Applies to any repo with a browser UI when a change touches a screen, control, or workflow. Use it with or without a screenshot QA harness. Consumers that run only backend jobs omit this file.
entries.scope: Any browser UI change; functional pass over affected screens, controls, and workflows

rules.title: Module context
rules.content:
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to any repo with a browser UI when a change touches a screen, control, or workflow. Use it with or without a screenshot QA harness. Consumers that run only backend jobs omit this file.

rules.title: Write one coverage matrix before the pass
rules.content: 1. **Write one coverage matrix before the pass** — One row for every affected route, control, mutation, state (empty, loading, error), and viewport. Each row carries the URL, the observed result, and evidence: a screenshot, console output, or network status. Use the shape `route | control | before → after | URL | evidence | width`. "Walk every tab" is not a bound; "every affected row has evidence" is. Completion criterion: no cell is blank.

rules.title: Walk the workflow from entry to result
rules.content: 2. **Walk the workflow from entry to result** — Sign in as the fixture persona, open the entry route, use the control, submit the mutation, read the resulting state, and sign out. Completion criterion: each mutation row records the state before, the state after, and the final URL.

rules.title: Capture both browser views in the same pass
rules.content: 3. **Capture both browser views in the same pass** — Use browse MCP for the signed-in session, navigation, tabs, and dialogs. Use chrome-devtools MCP for console errors, network statuses, and forced failure states. Completion criterion: the matrix records zero console errors and the expected status for every API call; a known failure has a reason and a linked row.

rules.title: Include the supported widths
rules.content: 4. **Include the supported widths** — Record 1280px and 768px rows when layout, navigation, or dialogs change; include the menu path at narrow widths. Completion criterion: each affected route has a narrow-width row.

rules.title: Send the matrix with the diff for review
rules.content: 5. **Send the matrix with the diff for review** — A UI change without a matrix is incomplete. The reviewer checks for missing rows and asks for the absent evidence; this is a judgement call, not a lint rule.

entries.title: Test Rules — determinism, low-value tests and comment audits
entries.name: Test Rules — determinism, low-value tests and comment audits
entries.description: Applies to repos where CI runs a test command under a pinned runtime version, and to any repo running a test/comment-code audit. This module carries both the rules and the audit procedure. Consumers without a CI test job or a test/comment audit omit this file.
entries.scope: Test determinism, low-value test and comment-code audits, with the audit procedure

rules.title: Module context
rules.content:
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to repos where CI runs a test command under a pinned runtime version, and to any repo running a test/comment-code audit. This module carries both the rules and the audit procedure. Consumers without a CI test job or a test/comment audit omit this file.

rules.title: Every source file gets a verdict
rules.content: 1. **Every source file gets a verdict** — `clean` or one or more findings with `file:line` evidence.

rules.title: Report before fixing
rules.content: 2. **Report before fixing** — present the merged report and wait for approval before editing. Re-run format, lint, typecheck, and tests after applying fixes.

rules.title: Re-verify
rules.content: 3. **Re-verify** dead-code and unused-symbol claims with a repo-wide exact-word count before flagging (re-exports and test seams count as live).

rules.title: Slice-type checks
rules.content: 4. **Slice-type checks** still apply: frontend, Prisma, API, i18n, fixtures, e2e per `rules/audit.md` #18.

rules.title: Low-value test scope
rules.content:
4a. **Low-value test scope** — Apply this audit criterion:

A test is low-value when it fails to catch a real regression. Flag and fix:

rules.title: No assertions
rules.content: 5. **No assertions** — a test body with zero `expect`/`assert`.

rules.title: Tautologies
rules.content: 6. **Tautologies** — `expect(true).toBe(true)`, or comparing a value to itself or to a recomputation of the same input.

rules.title: Mock-echoes
rules.content: 7. **Mock-echoes** — asserting a mock returns the value it was stubbed to return.

rules.title: Mock-wiring
rules.content: 8. **Mock-wiring** — asserting only that a stubbed collaborator was called with stubbed args; no behavior exercised.

rules.title: Trivial projections
rules.content: 9. **Trivial projections** — asserting a mapper copies fields 1:1 with no branching, transformation, or boundary.

rules.title: Constant pins
rules.content: 10. **Constant pins** — asserting a named constant equals its literal value; cover the threshold through behavior instead.

rules.title: Weak assertions
rules.content: 11. **Weak assertions** — `typeof x === "string"` for every element, `.toHaveLength(1)` with no shape check, `.success` booleans only.

rules.title: Repeated scripted cases
rules.content: 12. **Repeated scripted cases** — multiple tests asserting the identical branch for distinct but equivalent inputs; collapse to a table-driven case.

rules.title: Single-branch gates
rules.content:
13. **Single-branch gates** — a boolean gate tested on one of four combinations.

Fix rule: **never just delete coverage for live behavior.** Replace a slop test with a behavioral test in the same pass; deletion is allowed only when the scenario is a duplicate or a constant pin with no behavior to assert.

rules.title: Narrating comments
rules.content: 14. **Narrating comments** — comments that restate the adjacent line or narrate obvious steps. Keep intent, rationale, gotchas, and non-obvious invariants.

rules.title: Commented-out code
rules.content: 15. **Commented-out code** — dead blocks left in source; delete them.

rules.title: Suppression directives without reason
rules.content: 16. **Suppression directives without reason** — inline `eslint-disable`/`oxlint-disable`/`ts-ignore` with no blocker reason, and file-level disables. Fix the code, or move a legitimate carve-out into a scoped config `overrides` block with a reason comment.

rules.title: Run the gate with the CI-pinned runtime before push
rules.content: 17. **Run the gate with the CI-pinned runtime before push** — Use `npx -y bun@<pinned version> run verify` (or the Node version in `package.json#engines`), not the local binary. A local canary build hides stable-only failures. Completion: the gate passes under the same version CI installs. Precedent: Graveshift 2026-11 — local Bun canary passed 1336 tests; CI Bun 1.4.4 stable found four failures.

rules.title: Read failed CI checks before editing code
rules.content: 18. **Read failed CI checks before editing code** — Run `gh run view <id> --log-failed` and reproduce with the pinned runtime. Completion: each red check has a named root cause before a fix is written.

rules.title: Spawn test children with an env allowlist
rules.content: 19. **Spawn test children with an env allowlist** — Pass `PATH` and the named boot variables only. Forwarding `process.env` leaks runner variables and secrets into the child and can stop boot. Completion: the child receives only listed names. Precedent: Graveshift 2026-11 — an MCP stdio smoke test exited in CI alone.

rules.title: Assert invariants, not incidental layout
rules.content: 20. **Assert invariants, not incidental layout** — Exempt paths the runtime controls, such as the directory holding `process.execPath`, from checks that reject host-home paths. Completion: the assertion still rejects every other host-home path.

rules.title: Parse recorded call arguments with a schema before asserting
rules.content: 21. **Parse recorded call arguments with a schema before asserting** — Do not read a property after `toMatchObject` with `expect.stringContaining`; Bun 1.4.4 stable mutates the received value to `{}`. Completion: assertions read a parsed copy.

rules.title: Use `%#` in `test.each` titles when inputs hold BigInt or complex values
rules.content: 22. **Use `%#` in `test.each` titles when inputs hold BigInt or complex values** — `%j` calls `JSON.stringify` and throws an unhandled error between tests while every test still reports pass. Completion: the table runs with zero unhandled errors.

rules.title: Run the gate in a clean runner-like environment before push
rules.content: 23. **Run the gate in a clean runner-like environment before push** — Use the pinned runtime with a fresh empty `TMPDIR` and a `PATH` that excludes local-only tools. A rich developer environment hides host-only temp paths and locally installed CLIs. Completion: the gate passes with the pinned runtime and the reduced environment. Precedent: owobot-tools 2026-11 — `mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'opencode', ...))` passed locally and failed on CI with `ENOENT`.

rules.title: Stub external CLI tools in tests
rules.content: 24. **Stub external CLI tools in tests** — A test must not require a host-installed binary. Inject a deterministic stub through the existing tool seam or a temp script. Completion: the test passes with that tool absent from `PATH`. Precedent: owobot-tools 2026-11 — an OCR conformance test needed ImageMagick 7, which the Ubuntu runner did not provide.

rules.title: Isolate test files that mock shared modules
rules.content: 25. **Isolate test files that mock shared modules** — Bun stable shares one module registry across test files. A mock in one file leaks into another and changes results by file order. Run the affected suite with `--isolate` when files mock the same module with different shapes. Completion: the suite passes under the pinned runtime with per-file isolation enabled, and no test depends on another file's mock. Precedent: owobot-tools 2026-11 — two TUI files mocked the settings client with different schemas; 11 tests failed on CI stable and passed with `--isolate`.

rules.title: Inventory → slices
rules.content: 26. **Inventory → slices** — List test files and source directories (`find`, `package.json` workspaces). Partition into slices: one package or directory subtree per subagent. Record every test path.

rules.title: Dispatch subagents
rules.content: 27. **Dispatch subagents** — Run one subagent per slice in parallel. Each prompt carries: the slice's paths, the relevant rules in this module, the report format below, and the slice type (frontend, API, package, worker). Each subagent returns a findings table. Completion criterion: every test file in the slice carries a verdict, and every finding cites `file:line`.

rules.title: Merge
rules.content:
28. **Merge** — Dedupe findings shared across slices. Merge into one table:

| Category | Location | Finding | Action | Status |
| -------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ------ |

Categories: `test` (low-value test), `slop` (narrating comment / commented-out code), `suppression`.

rules.title: Report gate
rules.content: 29. **Report gate** — Present the merged report. Wait for approval before editing.

rules.title: Implement
rules.content: 30. **Implement** — Apply fixes per the rules: replace slop tests covering live behavior with behavioral tests in the same pass; delete only duplicates and constant pins. Remove narrating comments and commented-out code. Remove or reason suppression directives; move legitimate carve-outs to scoped config overrides. Re-run format, lint, typecheck, and tests after applying. Update the audit file's status column.

2. **Report before fixing** — present the merged report and wait for approval before editing. Re-run format, lint, typecheck, and tests after applying fixes.
<!-- rule: re-verify -->
3. **Re-verify** dead-code and unused-symbol claims with a repo-wide exact-word count before flagging (re-exports and test seams count as live).
<!-- rule: slice-type-checks -->
4. **Slice-type checks** still apply: frontend, Prisma, API, i18n, fixtures, e2e per `rules/audit.md` #18.

## Low-value tests (`category: test`)

<!-- rule: low-value-test-scope -->
4a. **Low-value test scope** — Apply this audit criterion:

A test is low-value when it fails to catch a real regression. Flag and fix:

<!-- rule: no-assertions -->
5. **No assertions** — a test body with zero `expect`/`assert`.
<!-- rule: tautologies -->
6. **Tautologies** — `expect(true).toBe(true)`, or comparing a value to itself or to a recomputation of the same input.
<!-- rule: mock-echoes -->
7. **Mock-echoes** — asserting a mock returns the value it was stubbed to return.
<!-- rule: mock-wiring -->
8. **Mock-wiring** — asserting only that a stubbed collaborator was called with stubbed args; no behavior exercised.
<!-- rule: trivial-projections -->
9. **Trivial projections** — asserting a mapper copies fields 1:1 with no branching, transformation, or boundary.
<!-- rule: constant-pins -->
10. **Constant pins** — asserting a named constant equals its literal value; cover the threshold through behavior instead.
<!-- rule: weak-assertions -->
11. **Weak assertions** — `typeof x === "string"` for every element, `.toHaveLength(1)` with no shape check, `.success` booleans only.
<!-- rule: repeated-scripted-cases -->
12. **Repeated scripted cases** — multiple tests asserting the identical branch for distinct but equivalent inputs; collapse to a table-driven case.
<!-- rule: single-branch-gates -->
13. **Single-branch gates** — a boolean gate tested on one of four combinations.

Fix rule: **never just delete coverage for live behavior.** Replace a slop test with a behavioral test in the same pass; deletion is allowed only when the scenario is a duplicate or a constant pin with no behavior to assert.

## Comment code (`category: slop` / `suppression`)

<!-- rule: narrating-comments -->
14. **Narrating comments** — comments that restate the adjacent line or narrate obvious steps. Keep intent, rationale, gotchas, and non-obvious invariants.
<!-- rule: commented-out-code -->
15. **Commented-out code** — dead blocks left in source; delete them.
<!-- rule: suppression-directives-witho -->
16. **Suppression directives without reason** — inline `eslint-disable`/`oxlint-disable`/`ts-ignore` with no blocker reason, and file-level disables. Fix the code, or move a legitimate carve-out into a scoped config `overrides` block with a reason comment.

## Runtime parity & child processes (mandatory)

<!-- rule: run-the-gate-with-the-ci-pin -->
17. **Run the gate with the CI-pinned runtime before push** — Use `npx -y bun@<pinned version> run verify` (or the Node version in `package.json#engines`), not the local binary. A local canary build hides stable-only failures. Completion: the gate passes under the same version CI installs. Precedent: Graveshift 2026-11 — local Bun canary passed 1336 tests; CI Bun 1.4.4 stable found four failures.

<!-- rule: read-failed-ci-checks-before -->
18. **Read failed CI checks before editing code** — Run `gh run view <id> --log-failed` and reproduce with the pinned runtime. Completion: each red check has a named root cause before a fix is written.

<!-- rule: spawn-test-children-with-an -->
19. **Spawn test children with an env allowlist** — Pass `PATH` and the named boot variables only. Forwarding `process.env` leaks runner variables and secrets into the child and can stop boot. Completion: the child receives only listed names. Precedent: Graveshift 2026-11 — an MCP stdio smoke test exited in CI alone.

## Assertions (mandatory)

<!-- rule: assert-invariants-not-incide -->
20. **Assert invariants, not incidental layout** — Exempt paths the runtime controls, such as the directory holding `process.execPath`, from checks that reject host-home paths. Completion: the assertion still rejects every other host-home path.

<!-- rule: parse-recorded-call-argument -->
21. **Parse recorded call arguments with a schema before asserting** — Do not read a property after `toMatchObject` with `expect.stringContaining`; Bun 1.4.4 stable mutates the received value to `{}`. Completion: assertions read a parsed copy.

<!-- rule: use-percent-in-testeach-titl -->
22. **Use `%#` in `test.each` titles when inputs hold BigInt or complex values** — `%j` calls `JSON.stringify` and throws an unhandled error between tests while every test still reports pass. Completion: the table runs with zero unhandled errors.

## Runner environment (mandatory)

<!-- rule: run-the-gate-in-a-clean-runn -->
23. **Run the gate in a clean runner-like environment before push** — Use the pinned runtime with a fresh empty `TMPDIR` and a `PATH` that excludes local-only tools. A rich developer environment hides host-only temp paths and locally installed CLIs. Completion: the gate passes with the pinned runtime and the reduced environment. Precedent: owobot-tools 2026-11 — `mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'opencode', ...))` passed locally and failed on CI with `ENOENT`.

<!-- rule: stub-external-cli-tools-in-t -->
24. **Stub external CLI tools in tests** — A test must not require a host-installed binary. Inject a deterministic stub through the existing tool seam or a temp script. Completion: the test passes with that tool absent from `PATH`. Precedent: owobot-tools 2026-11 — an OCR conformance test needed ImageMagick 7, which the Ubuntu runner did not provide.

## Module isolation (mandatory)

<!-- rule: isolate-test-files-that-mock -->
25. **Isolate test files that mock shared modules** — Bun stable shares one module registry across test files. A mock in one file leaks into another and changes results by file order. Run the affected suite with `--isolate` when files mock the same module with different shapes. Completion: the suite passes under the pinned runtime with per-file isolation enabled, and no test depends on another file's mock. Precedent: owobot-tools 2026-11 — two TUI files mocked the settings client with different schemas; 11 tests failed on CI stable and passed with `--isolate`.

## Audit procedure

<!-- rule: inventory-slices -->
26. **Inventory → slices** — List test files and source directories (`find`, `package.json` workspaces). Partition into slices: one package or directory subtree per subagent. Record every test path.

<!-- rule: dispatch-subagents -->
27. **Dispatch subagents** — Run one subagent per slice in parallel. Each prompt carries: the slice's paths, the relevant rules in this module, the report format below, and the slice type (frontend, API, package, worker). Each subagent returns a findings table. Completion criterion: every test file in the slice carries a verdict, and every finding cites `file:line`.

<!-- rule: merge -->
28. **Merge** — Dedupe findings shared across slices. Merge into one table:

| Category | Location | Finding | Action | Status |
| -------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ------ |

Categories: `test` (low-value test), `slop` (narrating comment / commented-out code), `suppression`.

<!-- rule: report-gate -->
29. **Report gate** — Present the merged report. Wait for approval before editing.

<!-- rule: implement -->
30. **Implement** — Apply fixes per the rules: replace slop tests covering live behavior with behavioral tests in the same pass; delete only duplicates and constant pins. Remove narrating comments and commented-out code. Remove or reason suppression directives; move legitimate carve-outs to scoped config overrides. Re-run format, lint, typecheck, and tests after applying. Update the audit file's status column.

entries.name: File Upload & Object Storage — inline multipart + `@nestjs/storage`
entries.description: Applies to every project with file uploads or object storage (NestJS APIs + web/portal/miniapp clients). Uploads ride inline `multipart/form-data` on authenticated business endpoints — never a standalone upload controller. Backend storage runs on `@nestjs/storage` (`StorageDisk`: `LocalDisk`, `S3Disk` for AWS S3/R2/MinIO, `InMemoryDisk` for tests).
entries.scope: APIs and clients with file uploads / object storage

rules.title: Module context
rules.content:
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to every project with file uploads or object storage (NestJS APIs + web/portal/miniapp clients). Uploads ride inline `multipart/form-data` on authenticated business endpoints — never a standalone upload controller. Backend storage runs on `@nestjs/storage` (`StorageDisk`: `LocalDisk`, `S3Disk` for AWS S3/R2/MinIO, `InMemoryDisk` for tests).

> **Legacy note**: Repos not yet migrated to `@nestjs/storage` keep their single `StorageService` (`@aws-sdk/client-s3`) + `mediaUpload(fields, options)` interceptor until migrated in a dedicated PR.

rules.title: Native axios multipart helpers
No eager upload & encapsulated preview cleanup
rules.content: 2. **No eager upload & encapsulated preview cleanup** — Selected `File` objects travel with the form submit; never fire a pre-upload on file pick. Render previews through an encapsulated child component (`<PhotoThumbnail file={file} />`, `rules/frontend.md` #18) whose `useEffect` calls `URL.createObjectURL(file)` and revokes it on file change or unmount.

rules.title: Client pre-check is UX only
rules.content: 3. **Client pre-check is UX only** — Mirror the server's MIME/extension and size allowlist on the client for instant feedback; the server remains the security boundary.

rules.title: One `StorageModule` per app, disks instead of SDK clients
rules.content:
4. **One `StorageModule` per app, disks instead of SDK clients** — Register `StorageModule.forRoot()` / `forRootAsync()` once in `AppModule` (global). Services inject the default `StorageDisk`, a named `@InjectDisk('name')`, or `Storage`. Never instantiate `S3Client` in feature modules. Configure S3-compatible disks (`S3Disk`) with `region: 'auto'` (overridable via `S3_REGION`, default `auto`), `forcePathStyle: true`, and env-driven credentials (`S3_ENDPOINT`, `S3_BUCKET_NAME`, `S3_PUBLIC_URL`, `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`).
   - **Provider-neutral naming**: disks are S3-compatible and may target AWS S3, MinIO, Cloudflare R2, or others. Use `S3_*` env vars and provider-neutral code symbols (`s3Base`, `storageBase`, `bucket`); never `R2_*` / `r2Base` / `cloudflare*`. Derive the storage base URL from `S3_ENDPOINT` + `S3_BUCKET_NAME` (or a single `S3_BASE_URL`) instead of hard-coding a provider name.
   - **Prefer `uploadToDisk` over `memoryStorage`**: use `uploadToDisk({ disk, contentTypes, limits, key })` so bytes stream straight to the disk with magic-byte validation and no full-body buffering. Reserve `memoryStorage()` for the rare case where the handler must transform the whole buffer in memory; even then, keep the body small and bound `limits.fileSize`.

rules.title: Inline multipart on authenticated business endpoints via `uploadToDisk`
rules.content:
5. **Inline multipart on authenticated business endpoints via `uploadToDisk`** — Attach `FileInterceptor` / `FileFieldsInterceptor` backed by `uploadToDisk({ disk, contentTypes, cacheControl })` (or the repo's `mediaUpload` interceptor) directly on the guarded business route (`@UseGuards(...)`):
   - **Magic-byte validation**: content type is detected from file bytes (`detectContentType`), paired with extension canonicalization (`EXT_TO_MIME` for ZIP-container formats like DOCX) and per-file size limits (default 10 MB → 413/400) before storage, leaving no partial files.
   - **Server-decided keys**: keys are generated server-side (`<folder>/<randomUUID()>.<ext>`); clients never control paths or filenames.
   - **No public `/uploads/*` endpoint**: uploads always ride an authenticated domain route. For exceptional direct-to-storage flows, use `signedUpload` + `receiveSignedUpload` + `detectContentType`.

rules.title: URL/key injection before `ValidationPipe`
rules.content: 6. **URL/key injection before `ValidationPipe`** — When using `mediaUpload(fields, options)` (`{ name, maxCount, folder?, bodyKey? }`), uploaded URLs inject into `req.body` before `ValidationPipe` so DTOs validate `@IsOptional() @IsUrl()` (`string`) or `@IsArray() @IsUrl({}, { each: true })` (`string[]`). Use `UploadFile` (local Multer subset interface) rather than global `Express.Multer.File`.

rules.title: Serving & private files
rules.content: 7. **Serving & private files** — Stream stored files via `serveFile(disk, file, { req, res, disposition })` (handles `Range` + `ETag`). Serve private files via time-limited `signedUrl` (and `serveSignedUrl` in dev).

rules.title: Swagger matches the wire format
rules.content: 8. **Swagger matches the wire format** — Decorate multipart handlers with `@ApiConsumes('multipart/form-data')` and `@ApiBody(multipartBody(fileFields, textFields))` so OpenAPI documents `format: binary` fields alongside text fields.

rules.title: Tests use `InMemoryDisk`
rules.content: 9. **Tests use `InMemoryDisk`** — Override `STORAGE_MODULE_OPTIONS` with `InMemoryDisk` instances and assert via `disk.keys()` / `disk.getBuffer(key)` — never touch the real filesystem or S3 in specs.

rules.title: Create
rules.content: 10. **Create** — Upload via interceptor/disk and persist the resulting URL(s)/key(s) in the DB row.

rules.title: Replace (update): persist first, fire-and-forget GC second
rules.content: 11. **Replace (update): persist first, fire-and-forget GC second** — Update the DB row with the new URL(s)/key(s) **first**, then fire-and-forget deletion of dropped media (`void disk.delete(oldKey)` or `void this.storage.deleteDropped(oldUrls, keptUrls)`). Never `await` cleanup — a failed delete must never fail a committed business update.

rules.title: Entity delete
rules.content: 12. **Entity delete** — Delete the DB row first, then fire-and-forget deletion of its media keys/URLs. Guard URL-to-key extraction so only objects on our storage host are deleted.

rules.title: Accept mid-update orphans
rules.content: 13. **Accept mid-update orphans** — If the upload succeeds but the subsequent DB write fails, leave the orphaned object in the bucket for batch GC; never add compensating deletes in error paths.
