# File Upload & Object Storage — inline multipart + `@nestjs/storage`

<!-- rule: module-context -->
0. **Module context** — Apply this context when the module applies.

Applies to every project with file uploads or object storage (NestJS APIs + web/portal/miniapp clients). Uploads ride inline `multipart/form-data` on authenticated business endpoints — never a standalone upload controller. Backend storage runs on `@nestjs/storage` (`StorageDisk`: `LocalDisk`, `S3Disk` for AWS S3/R2/MinIO, `InMemoryDisk` for tests).

> **Legacy note**: Repos not yet migrated to `@nestjs/storage` keep their single `StorageService` (`@aws-sdk/client-s3`) + `mediaUpload(fields, options)` interceptor until migrated in a dedicated PR.

## Client (web, portal, miniapp)

<!-- rule: native-axios-multipart-helpe -->
1. **Native axios multipart helpers** — Call `api.postForm<T>()` / `api.putForm<T>()` / `api.patchForm<T>()` with a typed payload mixing `File` and scalar fields; never hand-roll `toFormData`:

   ```ts
   const { data } = await api.postForm<MyVideo>('/trainers/me/videos', {
     title,
     thumbnail, // File — rides with the form submit
     tags,      // string[] — repeated per key
   });
   ```

<!-- rule: no-eager-upload-and-encapsul -->
2. **No eager upload & encapsulated preview cleanup** — Selected `File` objects travel with the form submit; never fire a pre-upload on file pick. Render previews through an encapsulated child component (`<PhotoThumbnail file={file} />`, `rules/frontend.md` #18) whose `useEffect` calls `URL.createObjectURL(file)` and revokes it on file change or unmount.
<!-- rule: client-pre-check-is-ux-only -->
3. **Client pre-check is UX only** — Mirror the server's MIME/extension and size allowlist on the client for instant feedback; the server remains the security boundary.

## Server (`@nestjs/storage` + NestJS)

<!-- rule: one-storagemodule-per-app-di -->
4. **One `StorageModule` per app, disks instead of SDK clients** — Register `StorageModule.forRoot()` / `forRootAsync()` once in `AppModule` (global). Services inject the default `StorageDisk`, a named `@InjectDisk('name')`, or `Storage`. Never instantiate `S3Client` in feature modules. Configure S3-compatible disks (`S3Disk`) with `region: 'auto'` (overridable via `S3_REGION`, default `auto`), `forcePathStyle: true`, and env-driven credentials (`S3_ENDPOINT`, `S3_BUCKET_NAME`, `S3_PUBLIC_URL`, `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`).
   - **Provider-neutral naming**: disks are S3-compatible and may target AWS S3, MinIO, Cloudflare R2, or others. Use `S3_*` env vars and provider-neutral code symbols (`s3Base`, `storageBase`, `bucket`); never `R2_*` / `r2Base` / `cloudflare*`. Derive the storage base URL from `S3_ENDPOINT` + `S3_BUCKET_NAME` (or a single `S3_BASE_URL`) instead of hard-coding a provider name.
   - **Prefer `uploadToDisk` over `memoryStorage`**: use `uploadToDisk({ disk, contentTypes, limits, key })` so bytes stream straight to the disk with magic-byte validation and no full-body buffering. Reserve `memoryStorage()` for the rare case where the handler must transform the whole buffer in memory; even then, keep the body small and bound `limits.fileSize`.
<!-- rule: inline-multipart-on-authenti -->
5. **Inline multipart on authenticated business endpoints via `uploadToDisk`** — Attach `FileInterceptor` / `FileFieldsInterceptor` backed by `uploadToDisk({ disk, contentTypes, cacheControl })` (or the repo's `mediaUpload` interceptor) directly on the guarded business route (`@UseGuards(...)`):
   - **Magic-byte validation**: content type is detected from file bytes (`detectContentType`), paired with extension canonicalization (`EXT_TO_MIME` for ZIP-container formats like DOCX) and per-file size limits (default 10 MB → 413/400) before storage, leaving no partial files.
   - **Server-decided keys**: keys are generated server-side (`<folder>/<randomUUID()>.<ext>`); clients never control paths or filenames.
   - **No public `/uploads/*` endpoint**: uploads always ride an authenticated domain route. For exceptional direct-to-storage flows, use `signedUpload` + `receiveSignedUpload` + `detectContentType`.
<!-- rule: urlkey-injection-before-vali -->
6. **URL/key injection before `ValidationPipe`** — When using `mediaUpload(fields, options)` (`{ name, maxCount, folder?, bodyKey? }`), uploaded URLs inject into `req.body` before `ValidationPipe` so DTOs validate `@IsOptional() @IsUrl()` (`string`) or `@IsArray() @IsUrl({}, { each: true })` (`string[]`). Use `UploadFile` (local Multer subset interface) rather than global `Express.Multer.File`.
<!-- rule: serving-and-private-files -->
7. **Serving & private files** — Stream stored files via `serveFile(disk, file, { req, res, disposition })` (handles `Range` + `ETag`). Serve private files via time-limited `signedUrl` (and `serveSignedUrl` in dev).
<!-- rule: swagger-matches-the-wire-for -->
8. **Swagger matches the wire format** — Decorate multipart handlers with `@ApiConsumes('multipart/form-data')` and `@ApiBody(multipartBody(fileFields, textFields))` so OpenAPI documents `format: binary` fields alongside text fields.
<!-- rule: tests-use-inmemorydisk -->
9. **Tests use `InMemoryDisk`** — Override `STORAGE_MODULE_OPTIONS` with `InMemoryDisk` instances and assert via `disk.keys()` / `disk.getBuffer(key)` — never touch the real filesystem or S3 in specs.

## Media lifecycle

<!-- rule: create -->
10. **Create** — Upload via interceptor/disk and persist the resulting URL(s)/key(s) in the DB row.
<!-- rule: replace-update-persist-first -->
11. **Replace (update): persist first, fire-and-forget GC second** — Update the DB row with the new URL(s)/key(s) **first**, then fire-and-forget deletion of dropped media (`void disk.delete(oldKey)` or `void this.storage.deleteDropped(oldUrls, keptUrls)`). <!-- rule: entity-delete -->
12. **Entity delete** — Delete the DB row first, then fire-and-forget deletion of its media keys/URLs. Guard URL-to-key extraction so only objects on our storage host are deleted.
<!-- rule: accept-mid-update-orphans -->
13. **Accept mid-update orphans** — If the upload succeeds but the subsequent DB write fails, leave the orphaned object in the bucket for batch GC; never add compensating deletes in error paths.

entries.title: Claude Design Prompting & Production Audit Workflow
entries.name: Claude Design Prompting & Production Audit Workflow
entries.description: Interview the user to discover UI/UX design demand, generate multi-surface Claude Design prompts that open with the correct trigger prefix and balance creative freedom with production copy, responsive, and CRUD guardrails, audit .dc.html exports, and generate in-place patch prompts. Use when writing prompts for Claude Design or AI UI generators, grilling the user on app/portal features before design, or auditing a .dc.html archive for production readiness.
entries.scope: Grill the user on design demand, generate multi-surface Claude Design prompts (creative freedom + copy/responsive/CRUD guardrails), and audit `.dc.html` exports across CRUD, copy/UX, and responsive axes.

steps.title: Overview
steps.content:
# Claude Design Prompting & Production Audit Workflow

Turn product and domain requirements into a multi-surface prompt suite for Claude Design (`.dc.html`), give Claude Design maximum creative room to propose strong UX and visual patterns while locking down production copy, responsive reachability, and CRUD/state completeness, and audit `.dc.html` exports before handing off to `workflows/claude-design-to-nextjs.md`.

steps.title: Process
steps.content: ## Process

steps.title: 1. Recon domain & codebase
steps.content:
### 1. Recon domain & codebase

Inspect the repository before asking the user any questions:
- Read `DESIGN.md`, `GLOSSARY-MAP.md`, tier `GLOSSARY.md` files (`rules/frontend.md` #21, `rules/i18n.md` #8), `schema.prisma`, `docs/research/*`, and existing route/theme files (`globals.css`).
- Note every conflict between the user's request, `DESIGN.md`, the glossaries, and the schema (e.g. overloaded role names, `Dashboard` vs `Role Portal`, deprecated fee/status enums in `schema.prisma` vs settled domain rules in `GLOSSARY.md`).
- **Completion criterion**: every surface, role, status enum, and glossary-vs-schema conflict is inventoried; zero look-up-able questions remain.

steps.title: 2. Grill the design tree in rounds
steps.content:
### 2. Grill the design tree in rounds

Interview the user along the frontier (`❓ **Q1** - **<Title>**: ... ➡️ **Recommendation**: ...`), updating `GLOSSARY.md` (pure domain glossary) and `DESIGN.md` (aesthetic tokens, responsive rules, component naming, and the User-Facing Copy **Term table**) inline as decisions settle:

1. **Round 1 — Surface topology & ubiquitous language**:
   - Align surface and role names with `GLOSSARY.md` (e.g. `Public Landing Page`, `Auth Surface`, and one surface per role). Prefer natural consumer labels (`Trang Phụ huynh`, `Góc Học tập`, `Trang Gia sư`) over architectural nouns (`Cổng / Portal`, `Dashboard`).
   - Settle multi-actor account relationships (e.g. how a paying `Client` Parent links to or provisions a `Student` Learner login).
   - Settle external UX reference benchmarks (e.g. Duolingo, Airbnb, Wise, Stripe, or `frappe/lms` as UX/curriculum benchmarks rather than runtime dependencies).
   - Confirm prompt partitioning: **1 dedicated prompt per surface**, where Prompt 1 establishes `design/tokens.css` in the `design/` folder and Prompts 2..N inherit `design/tokens.css`.
   - Confirm stripping backend-only mechanics (webhooks, HMAC, cron internals, payment gateway brand names, internal SLA timers) from user-facing UI.
2. **Round 2 — Authority boundaries, commercial visibility & mutability (`U/D`)**:
   - Define cross-portal creation vs editing boundaries (e.g. Admin schedules `LMS Batch` cohorts; assigned Tutors co-author `LMS Course` chapters, lessons, and quizzes).
   - Define role-specific pricing visibility (e.g. `0₫` service fee on the Client invoice vs Gross Tuition − Platform Fee = Net Payout on the Tutor side).
   - Ask the **Mutability & Cancellation question**: which records can users **Update (`U`)** or **Cancel / Withdraw / Delete (`D`)** self-service vs after verification/approval (e.g. editing a `VERIFIED` Tutor profile, requesting a rank upgrade, editing or cancelling a `PENDING_REVIEW`/`PUBLISHED` class request, withdrawing a `PENDING` application, replacing a submitted homework file before grading).
3. **Round 3 — Copy tone, responsive targets, token freedom & delivery**:
   - Confirm whether Prompt 1 has full creative freedom to invent the visual identity (`design/tokens.css`) or must use existing CSS variables.
   - Confirm target UI copy language (`Tiếng Việt` consumer-grade copy, zero operator jargon, zero unverified marketing claims like `98% match`) and keep all statutory/legal disclaimers out of UI chrome (dedicated `/terms` and `/privacy` routes own legal copy per `rules/i18n.md` #11).
   - Confirm saving the prompt suite to `docs/drafts/claude-design-prompts.md` in addition to the chat response.
- **Completion criterion**: the design tree frontier is empty, the user confirms shared understanding, and `GLOSSARY.md` reflects every settled term.

steps.title: 3. Generate multi-surface prompts (Creative Freedom + Production Guardrails)
steps.content:
### 3. Generate multi-surface prompts (Creative Freedom + Production Guardrails)

Write one self-contained markdown prompt per surface in `docs/drafts/claude-design-prompts.md`. Balance **creative latitude** (letting Claude Design's design priors shine) with **non-negotiable production guardrails**:

- **Trigger prefix — open every prompt with the right one**: Claude Design sets the deliverable type from a fixed opening phrase. Selecting a template fills this phrase; the same phrase as the first pasted line selects that deliverable type. Use this map:

  | Template button | Trigger prefix |
  | --- | --- |
  | Blank | *(none)* |
  | Mobile app design | `Design a mobile app for` |
  | Slides | `Make a slide deck about` |
  | Document | `Write a document:` |
  | Wireframe | `Wireframe the screens for` |
  | Animation | `Animate` |
  | UI mockups | `Make UI mockups for` |
  | Résumé | `Make a résumé for` |
  | 3D object | `Model a 3D object:` |
  | Research | `Put together a research report on` |
  | HTML email | `Design an HTML email for` |
  | Color + type pairing | `Explore color and type pairings for` |

  - Use `Design a mobile app for` (Mobile app design) for every Step 3 surface prompt.
  - Select the matching template in Claude Design, then paste the prompt with the prefix as its literal first line. A wrong prefix yields the wrong deliverable (for example, a document instead of screens).

     - Write outcome-first copy in the end user's everyday language (`Trang Phụ huynh`, `Góc Học tập`, `Chuyển thu nhập`, `Đã nhận`, `Gợi ý phù hợp`, `Phản hồi trong 2 giờ`, `Tổng quan`, `Xác thực`, `Hồ sơ`, `Chuỗi ngày học`).

  2. **Prototype Control Isolation Guardrail (100% Clean Product Surface)**:
     - House all prototype state, persona, time-travel, and error-simulation switchers inside a single floating, collapsible **Prototype Toolbar** (`data-prototype-toolbar` at bottom-right) or `data-props` controls so the product canvas renders 100% production-authentic UI (keep demo quick-fill bars, OTP hint banners, `"Simulate >5m late"` switches, and `"Test >20MB file"` buttons out of product headers, cards, forms, and modals).

### 4. Audit `.dc.html` archive & generate in-place patch prompts

When inspecting a `.zip` export from Claude Design (or generating follow-up patch prompts for an existing archive/codebase):
1. **Extract once into sandbox**: if the `.zip` path sits outside the workspace (e.g. `~/Downloads/*.zip`), copy it to `/tmp/` or `<appDataDir>/brain/<id>/scratch/design/` in one step and `unzip -o` inside the sandbox.
2. **One-command `x-dc` structure scan first**: Claude Design `.dc.html` files store markup in `<x-dc>`, screen/modal names in `data-screen-label`, component props in `<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props="...">`, shared imports in `<dc-import>`, and conditionals in `<sc-if>` / `<sc-for>`. Never read multi-thousand-line `.dc.html` files chunk-by-chunk first. Run one index command across the extracted folder:
   ```bash
   rg -n 'data-screen-label=|data-props=|<dc-import|state\s*=|const\s+(NAV|TABS|ST|SEED|RANK)' *.dc.html data.js
   ```
3. **Audit across 3 Production Axes**:
   - **Axis A — Master CRUD & Lifecycle Matrix**: verify `Create (C)`, `Read (R)`, `Update (U)`, and `Delete / Cancel / Archive (D)` plus the 6-Point Completeness Contract across every domain entity.

steps.title: Overview
steps.content:
# Claude Design to Next.js/React Workflow

Convert Claude Design (`.dc.html`) exports to production Next.js/React code while enforcing `rules/frontend.md`, `rules/i18n.md`, and `rules/linting.md`.

steps.title: Process
steps.content: ## Process

steps.title: 0. Zip intake → `apps/<app>`
steps.content:
### 0. Zip intake → `apps/<app>`

When the input is a `.zip`, prepare the workspace before step 1:
- **Sandbox first**: copy the zip to the approved temp dir, hash it, and `unzip` outside the repo. Never unzip into the working tree; never edit the archive.
- **Scan once, then read ranges**: run the step-1 `x-dc` scan plus `rg -o 'style="|sc-if|sc-for|\{\{'`, and record counts for inline styles, off-grid px values, fractional font sizes, Unicode glyphs, iframes, CDN imports, and image slots.
- **Inventory before code**: map every screen/view and query parameter to a target route; mark design-only surfaces (component sheets, screen canvases, state catalogues, notes, device frames) as "do not ship".
- **Extract the contract**: write `design-contract.json` with tokens, type scale, spacing map, copy keys, icon map, screen map, data shapes, and the run state machine; mirror the decisions in `DESIGN.md`.
- **Scaffold before porting**: add `apps/<app>`, `packages/ui`, and `packages/i18n` to the workspace; prove `format:check`, `lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, and `build` are green with no design code. Fix the scaffold before charging a port failure.
- **Pick one pilot slice**: the densest interactive surface bound to a real artifact (data grid, calendar, review table), not the landing page. Convert that slice through steps 1–6 before scaling.
- **Completion criterion**: inventory, contract, green scaffold, and one slice chosen.

steps.title: 1. Design intake & workspace mapping
steps.content:
### 1. Design intake & workspace mapping

Inspect both the `.dc.html` markup and any companion `data.js` / `design/tokens.css` files (`rules/frontend.md` #20 — motion, timers, and computed display values live in `<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script>` and `data.js`, not HTML):
- **One-command `x-dc` scan first**: Claude Design `.dc.html` files store markup in `<x-dc>`, screen/modal names in `data-screen-label`, component props in `<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props="...">`, and shared imports in `<dc-import>`. (If the `.dc.html` archive has not been audited for full `C/R/U/D` and lifecycle state completeness yet, run Step 4 of `workflows/claude-design-prompting.md` first.)
- **Incremental drops (v2 `.zip`)**: extract to a sibling folder and run `diff -rq <old_dir> <new_dir>` + `diff -u` first so you only inspect changed screens/tokens.
- **Surface-to-workspace matrix**: run `find apps packages -maxdepth 2` to map each `.dc.html` file to its owning workspace app (`apps/web`, `apps/auth`, `apps/client`, `apps/student`, `apps/tutor`, `apps/admin`) and shared package entry points (`packages/ui`, `packages/shared`, `packages/contracts`, `packages/i18n`).
- **Animations**: extract `@keyframes` bodies and `animation:` use-counts by script (`rules/frontend.md` #19), never by eye.
- **Completion criterion**: `.dc.html` → `apps/*` / `packages/*` file matrix, component inventory, route map, and data model sketch produced.

steps.title: 2. Spec alignment
steps.content:
### 2. Spec alignment

Diff the design inventory against the product spec (e.g. `docs/specs/...`):
- Classify every discrepancy as **Missing** (in spec, absent in design), **Partial**, or **Wrong** (contradicts spec).
- **Completion criterion**: gap report presented and scope confirmed by the user before writing app code.

steps.title: 3. Domain modeling & `DESIGN.md` alignment
steps.content:
### 3. Domain modeling & `DESIGN.md` alignment

Cross-check all labels, statuses, component names, responsive layouts, and entity names against `DESIGN.md` and `GLOSSARY.md` (`rules/frontend.md` #21, `rules/i18n.md` #7–#8):
- Resolve overloaded terms, probe edge-case state transitions, keep `GLOSSARY.md` as a pure domain glossary, and update `DESIGN.md` (including its User-Facing Copy **Term table** and End-User vs Admin Console copy boundary) inline.
- **Completion criterion**: zero unresolved domain or UI copy terms; `DESIGN.md` and `GLOSSARY.md` updated.

steps.title: 4. Implementation
steps.content:
### 4. Implementation

Build each screen/slice adhering strictly to `rules/frontend.md` and `rules/general.md`:
- **Tailwind v4 cascade layers & `@source` (`rules/frontend.md` #5)**: never copy unlayered `* { margin: 0; padding: 0; }` resets or unlayered custom classes from `.dc.html` / `tokens.css` alongside `@import "tailwindcss"` (unlayered rules override every `@layer utilities` `p-*`/`m-*`/`mx-auto` class). Put element resets in `@layer base`, custom classes in `@layer components`, and add `@source "../";` + shared UI package `@source` paths in `apps/*/src/app/globals.css`.
- **≤250-line post-`bun fmt` file budget (`rules/linting.md` #9)**: `bun fmt` expands single-line JSX props, objects, and destructuring by 1.4×–2.5×. Author each view, modal, hook, and data file under ~250 lines and always run `bun fmt <paths>` *before* `bun lint --no-script --max-warnings=0 --allow-unsupported <paths>`.
- **Deep-module boundaries (`rules/frontend.md` #7)**: import workspace packages only via `package.json#exports` entry points and app-internal files directly by path; do not create `export *` folder barrels unless the repo uses the legacy barrel convention.
- **`.dc.html` mechanical translation gates (`lint:tokens`, `lint:icons`, `leak.test.ts`)**:
  - **No raw `#hex` or bracketed `[Npx]` utilities (`lint:tokens`, `rules/frontend.md` #6)**: `.dc.html` templates use inline hex and pixel styles (`style="background:#FFFCF6;font-size:13.5px"`). Translate every color and dimension to `@theme inline` semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens.css` (`bg-paper`, `bg-surface`, `border-line-strong`, `text-ink-3`, `bg-brand-700`, `bg-accent-600`, `font-serif`, `font-mono`) or `var(--am-*)`.
  - **Unicode glyphs → shared `ICON` vocabulary (`lint:icons`, `rules/frontend.md` #17)**: `.dc.html` templates draw icons as Unicode characters and emojis (`✓`, `×`, `→`, `★`, `♥`, `🔒`). Replace every JSX glyph with `<AmIcon icon={ICON.<concept>} size="sm|md|lg" />` (or `<AmRichIcon icon={RICH_ICON.<concept>} />` on decorative landing/empty cards) imported from `@scope/ui`. Keep arrows as characters only inside sentence strings (`"5.5 → 7.0"`, `↔`, `⇔`) and `<option>` bodies; strip leading `✓` glyphs from toast strings; add `aria-label` to every icon-only `<button>` or `<a>`.
  - **No prototype enum/machinery leaks or inline simulation chrome (`rules/i18n.md` #7, #10)**: strip raw enum badges (`PENDING_REVIEW`, `TRIAL_IN_PROGRESS`), internal terms (`SLA`, `Platform Fee`, `Billing Cycle`, `Tutor Rank`, `Portal / Cổng`, gateway brand mechanics like `qua SePay VietQR`, unverified `%` claims), and raw English UI loanwords (`Dashboard`, `Verify`, `Profile`, `Streak`, `Badge`) from `.dc.html` copy before adding strings to `packages/i18n`. Move any prototype state switchers (persona bars, time-travel pills, late/error simulation toggles, demo quick-fill buttons, OTP hints) into the floating `VercelFlagsToolbar` (`packages/ui`)—never render simulation controls inside product headers, forms, or modals.
  - **CSS-first responsive breakpoints, zero `window.innerWidth` layout flash**: translate `.dc.html` grids and shells to Tailwind v4 responsive utilities (`sm: 640px`, `md: 768px`, `lg: 1024px`, `xl: 1280px`). Never use `useState(1280)` + `window.innerWidth` resize hooks for layout switching (causes SSR/hydration flash on mobile) or un-breakpointed inline `style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "268px minmax(0, 1fr)" }}` on app shells, master-detail split panes, or multi-column forms/modals. Ensure every portal retains 100% navigation reachability below `1024px` and wraps `7×3` schedule/comparison grids in `overflow-x-auto`.
- **Data & forms (`rules/frontend.md` #3, #11–#13)**: use Ponytail mock hooks (`// ponytail: ... Upgrade if: ...` inside `useQuery`/`useMutation`) only when the API endpoint does not exist yet; wire real endpoints immediately when available. - **Route structure**: full-page create/edit uses a shared route editor across `/path/new` and `/path/[id]/edit` (`rules/frontend.md` #9); escape literal JSX entities (`'`, `"`, `<`, `>`).
- **Completion criterion**: `bun fmt`, `bun lint --no-script --max-warnings=0 --allow-unsupported`, `lint:boundaries`, `lint:tokens`, `lint:icons`, typecheck (`bun check` / `tsc --noEmit`), and unit tests pass with zero warnings.

steps.title: 5. Two-axis code review
steps.content:
### 5. Two-axis code review

Run `/code-review` against the base SHA along **Standards** (`rules/frontend.md`, `rules/i18n.md`, `rules/general.md`, Fowler smells) and **Spec** (missing, scope creep, wrong).
- **Completion criterion**: every finding resolved and re-verified with `bun fmt` + `bun lint --no-script --allow-unsupported`.

steps.title: 6. Live Chrome DevTools verification & UX refinement
steps.content:
### 6. Live Chrome DevTools verification & UX refinement

Verify the live rendered app against the `.dc.html` reference using Chrome DevTools MCP (`rules/frontend.md` #20):
1. `navigate_page(url)` and `list_console_messages(types: ["error"])` → confirm **0 runtime/hydration errors**.
2. `evaluate_script()` → assert `getComputedStyle(el)` box-model (`paddingTop`, `paddingLeft`, `marginLeft`, `maxWidth`, `width`, `backgroundImage`, `color`) on `<main>`, `<aside>`, and `<header>` matches the design (catches unlayered CSS reset collisions where `px-8 py-7` computes to `0px`).
3. `take_snapshot()` & `take_screenshot()` → verify spacing, typography, token colors, responsive breakpoints, keyboard/focus flows, loading/empty/error states, and both VI/EN locales for leaked untranslated words. (Save screenshots inside workspace-local `.tmp-screenshots/` and delete `.tmp-screenshots/` plus any Next 16 generated `apps/*/AGENTS.md` before committing.)
4. **Reach the states a fixture never produces** — `mock_network` a data route with a local fixture `body` (empty list / malformed payload) or an `upstream` stub returning 5xx or a dead endpoint, re-shoot, and audit the error/empty render against `rules/qa.md` #7/#8; `remove_network_mock` afterwards. When a runtime or hydration error from step 1 resists diagnosis, attach `set_logpoints` at the throwing source location (source-map resolved, output in `list_console_messages`) instead of editing in a `console.log` and waiting for a rebuild.
- **Completion criterion**: pixel-perfect computed layout verified in Chrome DevTools, 0 console errors, clean `git status`, and all verification gates green.

steps.title: Conversion method check
steps.content:
## Conversion method check

Before a full port, run the pilot slice twice from the same scaffold, fixture, and timebox:
- **Arm A — markup-first**: translate the `.dc.html` markup to JSX; clean tokens and icons only when a gate fails.
- **Arm B — contract-first**: write the contract first, then components against it; use the markup only to confirm geometry.

Measure rework cycles to first green, time to parity, first-run gate failures, and quality debt. Adopt the arm with fewer rework cycles. If parity RMSE differs by more than 0.015, the more accurate arm wins. Record the result in the PR or ADR. Do not average a failed hard gate into a score.

entries.title: Codebase Audit Workflow
entries.name: Codebase Audit Workflow
entries.description: Audit the whole codebase in parallel subagent slices against the team-rule checklist — rule compliance, AI slop, dead code, suppressed linters, type safety, test slop, production risk. Use when asked to audit the codebase, check team-rule compliance repo-wide, find and remove AI slop and dead code across the repo, or scan for leaked secrets and risky dependencies.
entries.scope: Full-codebase audit in package/directory slices against `rules/audit.md` (team-rule compliance, slop, dead code, risk, secrets).

steps.title: Overview
steps.content:
# Codebase Audit Workflow

Audit every source file against `rules/audit.md` using one subagent per slice,
then fix from an approved report. Use the rules MCP to load the checklist from
the rule index first.

steps.title: Process
steps.content: ## Process

steps.title: 1. Inventory → slices
steps.content:
### 1. Inventory → slices

List source directories and packages (`ls`, `package.json` workspaces). Partition them into **slices**: groups of paths that fit one subagent's context. One slice ≈ one package or directory subtree. Record every source path — the audit ends when each path sits in exactly one slice.

steps.title: 2. Dispatch subagents
steps.content:
### 2. Dispatch subagents

Run one subagent per slice, in parallel. Each dispatch prompt carries five things:

1. The slice's paths.
2. The checklist (paste the applicable `rules/audit.md` rules or their MCP IDs).
3. The report format below.
4. The slice's type (frontend, Prisma, API, i18n, or general) so the subagent applies the matching slice-type checklist entries.
5. The comment rubric in `rules/audit.md` #4, with a `file:line` verdict for every comment in the slice.

Each subagent returns a findings table for its slice. Its completion criterion: **every source file and every comment in the slice carries a verdict**, and every finding cites `file:line` evidence.

steps.title: 3. Merge
steps.content:
### 3. Merge

Dedupe findings that two slices share (one symbol flagged twice). Merge into one table:

| Category | Severity | Location | Finding | Fix |
| -------- | -------- | -------- | ------- | --- |

Categories come from the checklist: `slop`, `comment`, `suppression`, `test`, `dead-code`, `risk`, `rule`, `config-drift`, `library`, `ownership`.

steps.title: 4. Report gate
steps.content:
### 4. Report gate

Present the merged table plus a count per category and the total files audited. Wait for approval before editing anything.

steps.title: 5. Fix pass
steps.content:
### 5. Fix pass

On approval, apply fixes slice by slice. For `comment` findings: delete tautology and stale comments, delete excuse comments and file one aggregate issue, and promote a decision to an ADR only when it passes the three-test bar. After bulk comment edits, inspect the diff numstat and run `git diff --check`; expect only deletions and no whitespace-only lines. After all fixes: run lint, typecheck, and tests; the pass completes when they pass and the diff contains no new findings. Deleted dead code stays deleted — restore only what a failing test proves alive.

steps.title: 5a. Wave gates & two-axis review
steps.content:
### 5a. Wave gates & two-axis review

Do not run one large fix pass. Partition the approved findings into **waves** by dependency risk (safety → contracts → money → API boundaries → frontends → fixtures → deletions). Each wave lands in one commit per slice.

- **Per slice**: run the owning package's formatter, typecheck, lint, and targeted tests before moving on.
- **Per wave**: run the root gate (`bun fmt --check`, `bun lint`, `bun typecheck`, the full unit suite) and, where the repo has them, the composed API e2e and production builds.
- **Per wave review**: dispatch two read-only reviewers against the wave's fixed point. One checks **standards** (the repo's `rules/*.md` and design/copy contracts); one checks **spec** (the approved audit report and the plan). Each reports hard violations and judgement calls, quoting `file:line`.
- **Fix hard findings before the next wave.** Record a checkpoint with the fixed point and review range in the plan. A wave is done only when the root gate and both reviews are green.

This is the cheapest place to catch a wrong abstraction: the review agent has the diff and no exploration cost, while the implementation agent still holds the wave context.

steps.title: 6. Operating rhythm
steps.content:
### 6. Operating rhythm

Run when asked, or on a standing arrangement:

- **Tickets** — findings become issues per `rules/issues.md`: one issue per category batch, labeled `critical` (secrets, missing authorization), `high` (PII exposure, data-loss paths), or `normal`.
- **Scorecard** — append one line per run to `AUDIT.md` at the repo root: date, files audited, count per category. The trend is the deliverable.
- **Cadence** — quarterly full audits; weekly runs scope slices to paths changed since the last release tag.
- **Ownership** — every package in the inventory maps to a `CODEOWNERS` entry; unowned packages surface as findings under category `ownership`.

---
id: "wf-codebase-audit"
name: "Codebase Audit Workflow"
kind: "workflow"
description: "Audit the whole codebase in parallel subagent slices against the team-rule checklist — rule compliance, AI slop, dead code, suppressed linters, type safety, test slop, production risk. Use when asked to audit the codebase, check team-rule compliance repo-wide, find and remove AI slop and dead code across the repo, or scan for leaked secrets and risky dependencies."
scope: "Full-codebase audit in package/directory slices against `rules/audit.md` (team-rule compliance, slop, dead code, risk, secrets)."
priority: "mandatory"

# Codebase Audit Workflow

Audit every source file against `rules/audit.md` using one subagent per slice,
then fix from an approved report. Use the rules MCP to load the checklist from
the rule index first.

## Process

### 1. Inventory → slices

List source directories and packages (`ls`, `package.json` workspaces). Partition them into **slices**: groups of paths that fit one subagent's context. One slice ≈ one package or directory subtree. Record every source path — the audit ends when each path sits in exactly one slice.

### 2. Dispatch subagents

Run one subagent per slice, in parallel. Each dispatch prompt carries five things:

1. The slice's paths.
2. The checklist (paste the applicable `rules/audit.md` rules or their MCP IDs).
3. The report format below.
4. The slice's type (frontend, Prisma, API, i18n, or general) so the subagent applies the matching slice-type checklist entries.
5. The comment rubric in `rules/audit.md` #4, with a `file:line` verdict for every comment in the slice.

Each subagent returns a findings table for its slice. Its completion criterion: **every source file and every comment in the slice carries a verdict**, and every finding cites `file:line` evidence.

### 3. Merge

Dedupe findings that two slices share (one symbol flagged twice). Merge into one table:

| Category | Severity | Location | Finding | Fix |
| -------- | -------- | -------- | ------- | --- |

Categories come from the checklist: `slop`, `comment`, `suppression`, `test`, `dead-code`, `risk`, `rule`, `config-drift`, `library`, `ownership`.

### 4. Report gate

Present the merged table plus a count per category and the total files audited. Wait for approval before editing anything.

### 5. Fix pass

On approval, apply fixes slice by slice. For `comment` findings: delete tautology and stale comments, delete excuse comments and file one aggregate issue, and promote a decision to an ADR only when it passes the three-test bar. After bulk comment edits, inspect the diff numstat and run `git diff --check`; expect only deletions and no whitespace-only lines. After all fixes: run lint, typecheck, and tests; the pass completes when they pass and the diff contains no new findings. Deleted dead code stays deleted — restore only what a failing test proves alive.

### 5a. Wave gates & two-axis review

Do not run one large fix pass. Partition the approved findings into **waves** by dependency risk (safety → contracts → money → API boundaries → frontends → fixtures → deletions). Each wave lands in one commit per slice.

- **Per slice**: run the owning package's formatter, typecheck, lint, and targeted tests before moving on.
- **Per wave**: run the root gate (`bun fmt --check`, `bun lint`, `bun typecheck`, the full unit suite) and, where the repo has them, the composed API e2e and production builds.
- **Per wave review**: dispatch two read-only reviewers against the wave's fixed point. One checks **standards** (the repo's `rules/*.md` and design/copy contracts); one checks **spec** (the approved audit report and the plan). Each reports hard violations and judgement calls, quoting `file:line`.
- **Fix hard findings before the next wave.** Record a checkpoint with the fixed point and review range in the plan. A wave is done only when the root gate and both reviews are green.

This is the cheapest place to catch a wrong abstraction: the review agent has the diff and no exploration cost, while the implementation agent still holds the wave context.

### 6. Operating rhythm

Run when asked, or on a standing arrangement:

- **Tickets** — findings become issues per `rules/issues.md`: one issue per category batch, labeled `critical` (secrets, missing authorization), `high` (PII exposure, data-loss paths), or `normal`.
- **Scorecard** — append one line per run to `AUDIT.md` at the repo root: date, files audited, count per category. The trend is the deliverable.
- **Cadence** — quarterly full audits; weekly runs scope slices to paths changed since the last release tag.
- **Ownership** — every package in the inventory maps to a `CODEOWNERS` entry; unowned packages surface as findings under category `ownership`.

steps.title: Overview
steps.content:
# Lint Burn-down Workflow

A codebase that fires thousands of lint findings enforces nothing — the signal is gone. Burn the backlog to zero, then keep it there with a ceiling. This procedure was run end-to-end on a four-app monorepo (5.2k findings → 0, 78 rules un-parked, one surface at a time).

Use the rules MCP to inspect the `rules/linting.md` index. Load its applicable
rules and set the repo up per its scope and config rules.

steps.title: Doctrine: park → ratchet → un-park
steps.content:
## Doctrine: park → ratchet → un-park

1. **Set the ceiling** — each package's lint script runs `bun lint --no-script --max-warnings N --allow-unsupported .` at the current finding count. CI stays green and cannot regress.
2. **Ratchet** the ceiling down as tranches land. The ceiling stops debt from growing back; the config only reports.
3. **The ledger is one tracking issue** — never maintain finding counts in config comments (they go stale immediately).

steps.title: Baseline config
steps.content:
## Baseline config

Copy `configs/.oxlintrc.json` into the repo root (or root `oxlint.config.ts` in Ultracite repos):
- Permanent disagreements are **anti-goals**: set them `"off"` in config with a rationale comment (`typescript/parameter-properties` for NestJS DI, `unicorn/filename-case` for PascalCase components).
- Build/runtime conflicts (SWC decorator metadata, ES target limits, Next.js linter split) go into a scoped `overrides` block in config **with a reason** — off in config, never inline comments (`rules/linting.md` #10: baseline `bun lint` ignores inline `oxlint-disable-next-line` comments).

steps.title: Process
steps.content: ## Process

steps.title: 1. Measure → ledger
steps.content:
### 1. Measure → ledger

Run `bun lint --no-script --format json --allow-unsupported .`. Build the ledger as **rule × surface** (`api`, `web`, `miniapp`, `portal`, `scripts`, `packages`) with a total per rule in the tracking issue. A rule is un-parkable only when every surface reaches zero.

steps.title: 2. Set the ceiling and the scope
steps.content:
### 2. Set the ceiling and the scope

- Per package: `"lint": "bun lint --no-script --max-warnings N --allow-unsupported ."` — scope `.`, not `src`, so e2e specs, seeds, configs, and scripts are covered too. Exclude generated dirs once in `ignorePatterns`.
- Keep `lint-staged` active (`bun lint --no-script --fix --allow-unsupported` in `lint-staged`, then `bun fmt --staged` — fix-then-format, `rules/linting.md` #13). Never pass `--no-verify`.

steps.title: 3. Slices → waves of subagents
steps.content:
### 3. Slices → waves of subagents

Partition by directory into disjoint slices of ~60–140 findings (one directory = one subagent owner, 3–5 slices per wave). Every subagent dispatch enforces:
- Edit only your slice's files. Never run repo-wide fixers or `--fix-suggestions`.
- Run `bun fmt <paths> && bun lint --no-script --max-warnings=0 --allow-unsupported <paths>`, typecheck, and the slice's tests before reporting (`bun fmt` runs first because formatting expands lines 1.4×–2.5× and exposes `max-lines: 300` violations).
- Do not add inline `oxlint-disable-next-line` comments (ignored by baseline `bun lint`, `rules/linting.md` #10). Report genuine framework/target conflicts so the coordinator can record a scoped `overrides` entry in config; in ESLint/Ultracite profiles where directives run, use a single-line disable with `-- <reason>` only for true framework conflicts.
- Never weaken assertions or change runtime behavior to satisfy a rule.

steps.title: 4. Gates
steps.content:
### 4. Gates

- **After every wave**: run `bun fmt`, `bun lint --no-script --allow-unsupported`, full typecheck, and full test suite on the merged tree (`rules/general.md` #15). Re-count and rebalance the next wave.
- **Before the ceiling hits 0**: boot the real production build (`pnpm build && node dist/main.js` for NestJS; `next build` for Next.js) to verify DI metadata and Swagger schema generation at runtime, then run `format:check` and e2e suites.
- **One PR per surface/tranche** with the ratcheted ceiling, un-parked rules, and any ADR updates.

steps.title: 5. Close out
steps.content:
### 5. Close out

Delete each parked rule override as it hits zero, set every package ceiling to `--max-warnings 0`, and close the tracking issue with the final table.

steps.title: Hazards (all observed on a real burn-down)
steps.content:
## Hazards (all observed on a real burn-down)

| # | Hazard | Why green tests miss it | Guard |
| - | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Stripping annotations from decorated properties (`: boolean = false` → `= false`) | SWC emits `design:type` **only from explicit annotations**; Swagger crashes at boot | Keep annotations on decorated properties; boot the built app before shipping |
| 2 | `import type` for constructor-injected deps | Erased import → `design:paramtypes` is `undefined` → `UnknownDependenciesException` at boot | Keep value imports for DI; turn the specifier-style rule off for the API in config |
| 3 | Downgrading a rule with a bare `'warn'` | Replaces the config entry and **drops its options** (e.g. `namedComponents: 'arrow-function'`) | Repeat the rule's options array in every `warn` entry |
| 4 | Fix uses syntax above `tsconfig` `target`/`lib` | Named capture groups (ES2018) or `toSorted` (ES2023) fail downstream typecheck | Check `target`/`lib` first; use compatible syntax |
| 5 | Two linters on one surface (`bun lint --no-script --allow-unsupported` + `ESLint`) | Fixers fight over import specifiers and side-effect imports | Scope `lint-staged` and `bun lint --no-script --allow-unsupported` `ignorePatterns` per `rules/linting.md` #11, #13 |
| 6 | Removing a live barrel file | Breaks cross-repo importers | Count importers first; delete 0-importer barrels in place, migrate live ones in a dedicated slice |
| 7 | Blunt `--fix-suggestions` | Applies unsafe semantic rewrites (`toSorted` breaking in-place mutation callers) | Never use `--fix-suggestions`; fix per rule with tests as oracle |
| 8 | Running `bun lint --no-script --allow-unsupported` before `bun fmt` | `bun fmt` expands single-line JSX/objects past `max-lines: 300` at commit time | Always run `bun fmt` before `bun lint --no-script --allow-unsupported` (`rules/linting.md` #9) |

steps.title: Fix playbook (high-volume rules)
steps.content:
## Fix playbook (high-volume rules)

- **func-style / react/function-component-definition** — convert declarations to `const fn = (...) => {}` (preserve rule options when parked, Hazard 3).
- **require-await / promise/prefer-await-to-then** — drop `async` when no `await` exists (unless caller chains `.catch`/`.rejects` or interface requires `Promise`); convert `.then` chains to `async`/`await`.
- **require-unicode-regexp / prefer-named-capture-group** — add `u` flag and remove invalid escapes (`\-`, `\/`); check ES target before adding named capture groups (Hazard 4).
- **no-await-in-loop** — `Promise.all(items.map(...))` when independent; sequential-by-design loops get a scoped config override or single-reasoned directive.
- **vitest/max-expects / vitest/require-top-level-describe** — split into focused tests (never delete assertions); wrap hooks and tests in one top-level `describe`.
- **class-methods-use-this / typescript/no-extraneous-class** — convert stateless methods/classes to pure functions; NestJS `@Module()`/`@Injectable()` classes use `allowWithDecorator: true`.
- **typescript/no-non-null-assertion / eqeqeq** — replace `x!` with a guard, `??`, or typed test helper; replace `x == null` with `x === null || x === undefined`.

entries.title: QA Sweep Workflow
entries.name: QA Sweep Workflow
entries.description: Full UI/UX QA pass over a web product's frontends — bring up the stack with seeded data, screenshot every route at 3 device widths, vision-audit the PNGs with parallel review agents, fix presentational findings, and report a triaged list. Use when asked to QA the UI, run a screenshot sweep, audit responsive/UX issues across apps, or re-verify UI fixes with screenshots.
entries.scope: Full UI/UX QA pass: seeded stack, 3-device screenshot sweep, parallel vision audit, presentational fixes, triaged report.

steps.title: Overview
steps.content:
# QA Sweep Workflow

Screenshot every route of every frontend at desktop/tablet/mobile, vision-audit
the captures with parallel review agents, and fix presentational findings under
the applicable `rules/qa.md` rules loaded through the rules MCP.

Then report a triaged remaining-issues list. The reference run (VibeHost, 2026-10-25: 375 shots, ~35 findings, 2 fix rounds) shapes every step below.

steps.title: Process
steps.content: ## Process

steps.title: 1. Recon → target list
steps.content:
### 1. Recon → target list

Read the newest prior QA report (per-project QA notes or report doc) and `git log --oneline --since=<last QA date>` — every touched app or route gets extra audit attention. Read the sweep harness's `--help` before running it; the harness owns route lists, device profiles, seeded identities, and auth. **Completion criterion:** a written target list of apps, their ports, and the changed-since-last-pass routes.

steps.title: 2. Stack up with seeded data
steps.content:
### 2. Stack up with seeded data

Bring up the persistence layer, apply migrations, run the seed, start the dev servers **tee'd to a log file** — runtime errors are invisible in page status codes (a Next.js error boundary answers 200), and the log is how a server-side 500 hiding behind a rendered error page was found. **Completion criterion:** every app answers on its health endpoint.

Gotchas proven by incidents:

- Run the seed with the app's own env exported — a bare `bun run` may fall back to a different database port and seed nothing (or the wrong DB).
- A dev-server watch that recompiles can fail to rebind its port while the stale process keeps serving the OLD build — kill the listener before investigating 404s from new endpoints.
- Bundler persistent-cache panics (stale-task or chunk-group errors) are cured by deleting that app's build cache and restarting, not by code changes.
- Admin-style auth guards: if every privileged endpoint 403s for the seeded super-admin, the seed lost its identity-link rows — re-run the seed; never paper over with hand-minted tokens.

steps.title: 3. Sweep (3 devices × every route)
steps.content:
### 3. Sweep (3 devices × every route)

Archive the previous screenshot trees (before/after is half the audit's value), then run the harness **per app in parallel** — a serial sweep of ~400 routes takes ~40 min, parallel takes ~15. **Completion criterion:** manifests show every route shot with only expected status codes and zero failures.

**Manifest triage before any PNG is read**: statuses (5xx = infra), console errors per shot (a broken seed surfaces as 403s on every privileged call; empty-`src` images log per-row warnings; handled conflicts are noise), and final URLs (unexpected redirects mean the route list went stale). Fix infra before auditing — a sweep over a half-broken stack wastes the whole pass.

steps.title: 3a. Fault injection pass (mocked exception states)
steps.content:
### 3a. Fault injection pass (mocked exception states)

A seeded sweep only proves the happy path renders — the error UI is never exercised (`rules/qa.md` #16). Before the vision audit, force exceptions on one representative route per API surface through Chrome DevTools MCP: `mock_network` with a local fixture `body` (bad payload shape, empty list), or `upstream` redirected to a stub server returning the real 5xx status/headers or a dead endpoint (failed request). Configure mocks **before** navigating, then re-shoot the affected routes at all three devices and fold those PNGs into the step-4 target list — audit them against `rules/qa.md` #7/#8 (designed empty/error states, disabled silhouettes). Verify each mock actually hit (filter-less `mock_network` shows hit counts; service workers can bypass mocks), and `remove_network_mock` everything before any perf trace (mocks disable the HTTP cache and skew measurement). **Completion criterion:** every API surface has at least one mocked-failure PNG reviewed.

steps.title: 3b. Real-user functional pass
steps.content:
### 3b. Real-user functional pass

Run the functional browser pass under the applicable `rules/real-user-qa.md`
rules loaded through the rules MCP.

Use browse MCP for the signed-in session and chrome-devtools MCP for console and network evidence; record both in one coverage matrix. **Completion criterion:** every affected route, control, mutation, state, and viewport has a row with URL, result, and evidence.

steps.title: 4. Vision audit (parallel review agents)
steps.content:
### 4. Vision audit (parallel review agents)

Fan out read-only review agents over app sections — **at most 2 concurrently** (the environment's concurrency limit; a third bounces), each reading ≤ ~90 PNGs plus its manifest slice. The dispatch prompt carries: the design-system context, audit criteria (overflow/clipping at mobile, tab/scroll affordance, empty/error states, spacing/contrast, locale bugs), the expected states NOT to flag (404 variants, banned-identity errors, seeded placeholder data), and the **downscale rule**: full-page PNGs are downscaled during review — a copy claim from unreadable pixels is filed as low-confidence, never asserted. Name the previously retracted misreads so agents do not rediscover them. **Completion criterion:** every route reviewed; every finding cites the PNG and either names a source location or is marked low-confidence.

steps.title: 5. Verify → classify
steps.content:
### 5. Verify → classify

Re-verify each agent finding in the DOM or source before fixing (three of one run's findings were pixel misreads; ground truth is the DOM). Classify: **small** = presentational (fix under `rules/qa.md` without asking); **big** = layout restructure, new components, nav/IA, API behavior (present to the owner with evidence — never fixed silently). **Completion criterion:** a tagged findings list.

steps.title: 6. Fix loop
steps.content:
### 6. Fix loop

Fix smalls; keep both lint and typecheck green (new user-facing copy needs every locale's catalog or the i18n key check fails); reshoot the affected routes and read the PNG — a fix is done when the screenshot shows it. **Completion criterion:** gates green + reshoots confirm each fix.

steps.title: 7. Report
steps.content:
### 7. Report

Update the project's QA report: fixed items, verified-not-bugs (retracted misreads, so they are not rediscovered), and a triaged remaining list — backend slices / polish batch / needs-DOM-check / environment. Big items go to the owner as a decision list; hand off the remainder if the session ends mid-list. **Completion criterion:** the report names every open item with its triage bucket.

steps.title: Suggested skills
steps.content:
## Suggested skills

Invoke these through the Skill tool at the phase named; availability varies by consumer, so treat a missing skill as a pointer to the technique, not a blocker.

| Phase | Skill | Why |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |

name: "QA Sweep Workflow"
kind: "workflow"
description: "Full UI/UX QA pass over a web product's frontends — bring up the stack with seeded data, screenshot every route at 3 device widths, vision-audit the PNGs with parallel review agents, fix presentational findings, and report a triaged list. Use when asked to QA the UI, run a screenshot sweep, audit responsive/UX issues across apps, or re-verify UI fixes with screenshots."
scope: "Full UI/UX QA pass: seeded stack, 3-device screenshot sweep, parallel vision audit, presentational fixes, triaged report."
priority: "mandatory"

# QA Sweep Workflow

Screenshot every route of every frontend at desktop/tablet/mobile, vision-audit
the captures with parallel review agents, and fix presentational findings under
the applicable `rules/qa.md` rules loaded through the rules MCP.

Then report a triaged remaining-issues list. The reference run (VibeHost, 2026-10-25: 375 shots, ~35 findings, 2 fix rounds) shapes every step below.

## Process

### 1. Recon → target list

Read the newest prior QA report (per-project QA notes or report doc) and `git log --oneline --since=<last QA date>` — every touched app or route gets extra audit attention. Read the sweep harness's `--help` before running it; the harness owns route lists, device profiles, seeded identities, and auth. **Completion criterion:** a written target list of apps, their ports, and the changed-since-last-pass routes.

### 2. Stack up with seeded data

Bring up the persistence layer, apply migrations, run the seed, start the dev servers **tee'd to a log file** — runtime errors are invisible in page status codes (a Next.js error boundary answers 200), and the log is how a server-side 500 hiding behind a rendered error page was found. **Completion criterion:** every app answers on its health endpoint.

Gotchas proven by incidents:

- Run the seed with the app's own env exported — a bare `bun run` may fall back to a different database port and seed nothing (or the wrong DB).
- A dev-server watch that recompiles can fail to rebind its port while the stale process keeps serving the OLD build — kill the listener before investigating 404s from new endpoints.
- Bundler persistent-cache panics (stale-task or chunk-group errors) are cured by deleting that app's build cache and restarting, not by code changes.
- Admin-style auth guards: if every privileged endpoint 403s for the seeded super-admin, the seed lost its identity-link rows — re-run the seed; never paper over with hand-minted tokens.

### 3. Sweep (3 devices × every route)

Archive the previous screenshot trees (before/after is half the audit's value), then run the harness **per app in parallel** — a serial sweep of ~400 routes takes ~40 min, parallel takes ~15. **Completion criterion:** manifests show every route shot with only expected status codes and zero failures.

**Manifest triage before any PNG is read**: statuses (5xx = infra), console errors per shot (a broken seed surfaces as 403s on every privileged call; empty-`src` images log per-row warnings; handled conflicts are noise), and final URLs (unexpected redirects mean the route list went stale). Fix infra before auditing — a sweep over a half-broken stack wastes the whole pass.

### 3a. Fault injection pass (mocked exception states)

A seeded sweep only proves the happy path renders — the error UI is never exercised (`rules/qa.md` #16). Before the vision audit, force exceptions on one representative route per API surface through Chrome DevTools MCP: `mock_network` with a local fixture `body` (bad payload shape, empty list), or `upstream` redirected to a stub server returning the real 5xx status/headers or a dead endpoint (failed request). Configure mocks **before** navigating, then re-shoot the affected routes at all three devices and fold those PNGs into the step-4 target list — audit them against `rules/qa.md` #7/#8 (designed empty/error states, disabled silhouettes). Verify each mock actually hit (filter-less `mock_network` shows hit counts; service workers can bypass mocks), and `remove_network_mock` everything before any perf trace (mocks disable the HTTP cache and skew measurement). **Completion criterion:** every API surface has at least one mocked-failure PNG reviewed.

### 3b. Real-user functional pass

Run the functional browser pass under the applicable `rules/real-user-qa.md`
rules loaded through the rules MCP.

Use browse MCP for the signed-in session and chrome-devtools MCP for console and network evidence; record both in one coverage matrix. **Completion criterion:** every affected route, control, mutation, state, and viewport has a row with URL, result, and evidence.

### 4. Vision audit (parallel review agents)

Fan out read-only review agents over app sections — **at most 2 concurrently** (the environment's concurrency limit; a third bounces), each reading ≤ ~90 PNGs plus its manifest slice. The dispatch prompt carries: the design-system context, audit criteria (overflow/clipping at mobile, tab/scroll affordance, empty/error states, spacing/contrast, locale bugs), the expected states NOT to flag (404 variants, banned-identity errors, seeded placeholder data), and the **downscale rule**: full-page PNGs are downscaled during review — a copy claim from unreadable pixels is filed as low-confidence, never asserted. Name the previously retracted misreads so agents do not rediscover them. **Completion criterion:** every route reviewed; every finding cites the PNG and either names a source location or is marked low-confidence.

### 5. Verify → classify

Re-verify each agent finding in the DOM or source before fixing (three of one run's findings were pixel misreads; ground truth is the DOM). Classify: **small** = presentational (fix under `rules/qa.md` without asking); **big** = layout restructure, new components, nav/IA, API behavior (present to the owner with evidence — never fixed silently). **Completion criterion:** a tagged findings list.

### 6. Fix loop

Fix smalls; keep both lint and typecheck green (new user-facing copy needs every locale's catalog or the i18n key check fails); reshoot the affected routes and read the PNG — a fix is done when the screenshot shows it. **Completion criterion:** gates green + reshoots confirm each fix.

### 7. Report

Update the project's QA report: fixed items, verified-not-bugs (retracted misreads, so they are not rediscovered), and a triaged remaining list — backend slices / polish batch / needs-DOM-check / environment. Big items go to the owner as a decision list; hand off the remainder if the session ends mid-list. **Completion criterion:** the report names every open item with its triage bucket.

## Suggested skills

Invoke these through the Skill tool at the phase named; availability varies by consumer, so treat a missing skill as a pointer to the technique, not a blocker.

| Phase | Skill | Why |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 2 (stack up) | `diagnosing-bugs` | The rebind/cache/403 traps are misdiagnosis magnets — structured root-cause before touching anything. |
| 2–3 (sweep) | `webapp-testing` | Playwright harness patterns: server lifecycle, networkidle waits, element discovery when a route needs DOM inspection. |
| 3a (fault injection) | Chrome DevTools MCP | `mock_network` / `remove_network_mock` for mocked exception states (fixture `body` or a 5xx `upstream` stub); `set_logpoints` instead of editing in `console.log` while diagnosing. |
| 5 (verify → classify) | `diagnosing-bugs` | The DOM checks behind low-confidence findings are runtime inspections, not pixel reads. |
| 6 (fix loop) | `building-components` | Component standards for the fixes: accessibility, composition, state, styling under the project's design system. |
| 7 (report) | `triage` | File backend-slice findings as issues with the repo's label workflow instead of leaving them in the report. |
| 7 (report) | `handoff` | Hand the remaining list to a fresh session with environment state when the pass ends mid-list. |
| after | `retro` | Fold new incidents back into this workflow and `rules/qa.md` so the next pass starts smarter. |

entries.title: Themed Codebase Audit
entries.name: Themed Codebase Audit
entries.description: Audit a codebase along three themes — dead code, duplicated business logic, over-complex logic — via parallel scans, then grill the user to a shared understanding and execute in one branch per wave. Use when asked to find dead code, find duplication, simplify complex logic, or run "an audit like that one". For full rule-compliance sweeps sliced by package, use codebase-audit instead.
entries.scope: Three-theme audit (dead code, duplicated business logic, complex logic) with a grill gate and wave branches.

steps.title: Overview
steps.content:
# Themed Codebase Audit

Three parallel theme scans, a grilling gate, then wave-branches. Fill the
bracketed variables per project before starting.

steps.title: 0. Variables
steps.content:
## 0. Variables

- `REPO` — absolute repo path. `STACK` — frameworks, package manager, workspace
  layout. `BASE` — base branch (usually `main`).
- Confirm the harness has: parallel subagents (or Task-style explore agents),
  `rg`, and the project's verify commands (typecheck / lint / format / test).

steps.title: 1. Scan (no edits)
steps.content:
## 1. Scan (no edits)

Dispatch 3 explore subagents in parallel, one per theme. Each returns findings
only — no code changes.

1. **Dead code** — orphan files, exported symbols with zero repo-wide
   references, dead models/fields, dead dependencies, commented-out code. Cap
   ~25, highest confidence first. Per finding: file, symbol, evidence as a
   reference count ("N files reference it"), confidence high/med/low.
2. **Duplicated business logic** — the same rule in 2+ places (status labels,
   state machines, validators, formatters, API clients, constants). Cap ~15,
   drift-risk first. Per finding: concept, every `file:line` range, whether a
   shared home already exists, drift risk, and whether drift has ALREADY
   happened (quote the differing values).
3. **Complex logic** — files past the repo's split threshold, deep nesting,
   long functions, dead error paths, single-use abstractions. Cap ~12. Per
   finding: file, function + lines, what makes it hard to read, a ONE-LINE
   simplification.

Verification rules (bind all three): verify every symbol with a repo-wide
exact-word reference count — scan confidence is not truth. Read snippets, never
diagnose from filenames. Re-exports and same-name locals count as live until
proven otherwise. Test helpers and spec seams are not dead code.

steps.title: 2. Grill gate
steps.content:
## 2. Grill gate

Merge the three reports and dedupe. Then interview the user in rounds: numbered
questions (`❓ Q1…`), each with a recommended answer (`➡️`). Gather facts with
grep/subagents — never ask anything look-up-able. Genuine decisions only
(canonical wording, scope cuts, risk calls). **No edits until the user confirms
shared understanding.**

steps.title: 3. Execute
steps.content:
## 3. Execute

One branch per wave off `BASE` (stacked or independent — state which):
dead-code deletions, dedupe + drift fixes, complexity simplifications.
Per-edit rules:

- Re-verify each deletion at edit time. A re-fetch that looks dead may be
  load-bearing for freshness after an intervening write — read the surrounding
  writes first; when in doubt keep it with a comment.
- After each wave: typecheck + lint + format + full suites green, then commit.
- Open one PR per branch when all waves pass.

steps.title: 4. Report
steps.content:
## 4. Report

Per branch: what was removed/unified/simplified, what was deliberately kept
(and why), what was deferred with the trigger for revisiting. Surface any CI
failure that is pre-existing on `BASE` separately from branch regressions —
verify by rerunning the failed job before blaming the diff.
